The 'epoch-rotate JWKS' half: new keys get 128-bit kids via the existing rotation mechanism (no new code); retiring 64-bit prevKeyId comparators is R3 (signet-3723b6). title: action/dist/index.js ships undici 6.25.0 with three unpatched advisories — the override never reached the committed bundle
description:
Found by empirical release audit (notme-c0a4f6), verified independently. LIVE SUPPLY-CHAIN EXPOSURE in an artifact two repos execute with an OIDC identity in scope.

pnpm-workspace.yaml declares `undici@<6.28.0: "^6.28.0"` and the lockfile resolves undici@6.28.0 — but the committed action/dist/index.js embeds undici@6.25.0. The bundle was built before the override landed and never rebuilt, so the fix for GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524 (response desync), GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5 (CRLF injection) and GHSA-v3r7-h72x-cjcm (cookie attribute injection) never reached the artifact consumers run. All three are medium severity, all patched in 6.28.0.

Verified locally: rebuilding with `pnpm run build` in action/ produces a bundle embedding undici@6.28.0, with 15 isValidHeaderValue guards vs 0 in the committed one; the diff is 768 undici-referencing lines and our own source is unchanged (identical setOutput calls). Consumers: notme's own gha-identity.yml pins e57c9ad, signet's pins 1ccd3b0 — BOTH pins must move after the rebuild or the fix reaches neither.

Why nothing caught it: `task worker:audit` is scoped `dir: worker` and never looks at action/, and no CI job rebuilds the bundle or diffs it against source.

FIX (the rebuild is done in this branch — see the follow-on commit; what remains is the durable gate): add a CI job that rebuilds action/dist and fails on any diff, so the bundle cannot drift from its lockfile again. That is the AC's "generated bundles" clause and the only durable fix.

comments.text:
Signet-side status for the half of this bead's acceptance criteria that names signet ("the `uses:` pins in notme's gha-identity.yml and signet's copy are advanced").

Signet's exposure, measured on main (6d51775) rather than assumed:
- The pin exists in exactly ONE place: .github/workflows/gha-identity.yml:118, agentic-research/notme/action@1ccd3b040fd3af0a437c003b4f3d5cc7a71af9f1 (main, 2026-05-18). Consumers are signet-resign.yml and, cross-repo, rig's deploy.yml.
- It runs with id-token: write in scope, so the exposure is real in signet's CI, not just upstream.
- It does NOT touch the release artifact-signing path. release.yml → .github/actions/sign-artifact builds signet's own cmd/sigstore-kms-signet in-repo and uses sigstore/cosign-installer; the notme action is never invoked there. That scoping is why signet classifies this as blocking for its resign/identity path and advisory for the v0.3.0 artifact train (docs/release/goal-zero-promotion.md §4) — not as a downgrade of the P0, which signet agrees with, but so neither side over- or under-states which paths are affected.

Signet's action is filed as signet-6d2bcd with a formal cross-repo dependency on this bead, so it appears as blocked rather than forgotten. It cannot proceed before this one: a pin cannot be advanced to a commit that does not exist yet. When the rebuilt bundle lands, signet will advance the pin and verify the shipped action/dist/index.js at that SHA directly rather than trusting the lockfile — which is the exact failure mode this bead documents (override declared, bundle stale).
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
THE SELF-PIN IS STALE BY FIVE COMMITS, measured — which makes the "advance the pins" clause of this bead concrete rather than precautionary.

.github/workflows/gha-identity.yml:129 pins notme's OWN action:
  uses: agentic-research/notme/action@e57c9ad9bb798b7f6e3336f1c60ae489ac8907cf # PR #9 squash, 2026-05-10

Commits touching action/ since that SHA — three already on main (69e1c47 #14, 3ee9292 #20, 98da3fc #23) and two on goalzero (49b6930 the undici rebuild, 9a723f1 the action.yml output fix). So the pin's own comment, "which is the current shipping state", has been FALSE since at least #14 landed. Same defect class this session keeps producing: a claim nothing verifies.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is the reason this bead is P0: notme's OWN CI runs the pre-fix bundle carrying the three undici advisories. Rebuilding action/dist was necessary and is not sufficient — the fix reaches nobody until this pin and signet's (1ccd3b0) both move.

IS SELF-PINNING WRONG? It is FORCED, not chosen. gha-identity.yml is a REUSABLE workflow invoked by other repos; a local `uses: ./action` would resolve against the CALLER's checkout, which has no action/ directory. An absolute SHA reference is the only form that works for external callers. (Worth confirming against current GitHub semantics before anyone "fixes" it by switching to a local path — that change would break signet.)

But the cost is real and is currently being paid. For a SELF-reference the SHA buys none of the security it buys for a third party: the threat is "someone else moves a tag under me", and we control this repo. What it does buy is DRIFT — workflow and action ship in the same commit, and pinning freezes them apart. Two live consequences: a PR that changes action/ gets CI running the OLD action, so the change cannot validate itself; and a security fix waits on a manual bump that nothing prompts.

RECOMMENDATION — do not unpin, make drift LOUD. Add a CI check asserting the pinned SHA equals the most recent commit touching action/ (and, once the bundle is rebuilt in CI, that the pinned commit's dist matches a fresh build). That would have caught this five commits ago, and it is the same shape as the gha-identity-outputs gate added earlier today: the pin is a claim, and nothing verified it. Fold this into this bead's existing "CI job rebuilds the bundle and fails on diff" clause rather than filing separately — they are the same gate.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
TWO OF THREE ACCEPTANCE CLAUSES NOW MET. Verified 2026-08-06 against HEAD, not inferred.

CLAUSE 1 — "action/dist/index.js embeds undici >= 6.28.0": MET. The committed bundle contains 6.28.0, which is the version GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524, GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5 and GHSA-v3r7-h72x-cjcm all name as patched. `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves `undici@6.28.0`; `pnpm audit --prod` reports no known vulnerabilities.

Worth being honest about HOW it got fixed: it was a side effect. The bundle was rebuilt today for an unrelated reason (the PoP pre-image fix, notme-a011d2), and that rebuild is what finally carried the override into the artifact. Nobody set out to close this. That is precisely the failure mode this bead describes — the override mechanism had already been corrected (moved to pnpm-workspace.yaml, since pnpm 10 stopped reading the `pnpm` field from package.json), the config looked right, audit was green, and the artifact two repos actually execute stayed vulnerable until something incidental rebuilt it.

CLAUSE 2 — "a CI job rebuilds the bundle and fails on diff": MET, and this is the clause that stops recurrence. New `task action:bundle-check`, wired into ci.yml's `check` job immediately after `worker:audit`. The two are complementary and the distinction matters: AUDIT READS THE LOCKFILE, THE GATE READS THE ARTIFACT. They can disagree, and for weeks they did — audit never looks at action/dist/index.js, which is the file `uses: agentic-research/notme/action@<sha>` actually executes, because GitHub runs the checked-in bundle rather than building it.

Deliberately a DIFF rather than rebuild-and-commit: a job that silently fixed the bundle would conceal that sources and artifact were pushed out of step, which is the signal worth keeping.

WATCHED IT FAIL FIRST, and the first attempt is worth recording. The initial probe appended an unused `const` to action/src/index.ts and the gate PASSED — correctly, because esbuild tree-shakes it and the bundle was byte-identical. A side-effecting probe (`console.log`) produced the real failure with the intended message. So the gate tracks THE ARTIFACT, not the source text. That is the right granularity — "the shipped bundle changed" is the question that matters — but it means a source edit that optimises away will not trip it, which is correct and should not be mistaken for a hole.

CLAUSE 3 — "the `uses:` pins in notme's gha-identity.yml and signet's copy are advanced to a commit containing the rebuilt bundle": NOT MET, and not doable from here. The pin bump requires the rebuilt bundle to exist on `main`, and per the branch model this repo does ONE merge (goalzero → main) rather than per-feature PRs. Signet's copy is theirs to advance. `task pin:check` currently reports the self-reference serving the same code as origin/main, so the pin is not stale TODAY — it will become stale the moment goalzero merges, and that is when both pins move.

BEAD STAYS OPEN on clause 3 alone. The live supply-chain exposure is closed; what remains is pin propagation across the merge.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: action/dist/index.js embeds undici >= 6.28.0; a CI job rebuilds the bundle and fails on diff; the `uses:` pins in notme's gha-identity.yml and signet's copy are advanced to a commit containing the rebuilt bundle.

title: Staging mints tokens claiming iss: https://auth.notme.bot — ISSUER is a module constant on both mint and verify
description:
Found by trust-root review of the staging environment (goal notme-cf288e). worker/src/auth/token.ts:16 `const ISSUER = "https://auth.notme.bot"` is used at :64 for every minted token AND at :133 for validateClaims.

The discovery documents ARE env-derived (worker.ts:2874), so staging advertises `issuer: https://auth-staging.notme.bot` and then mints tokens asserting the PRODUCTION issuer, signed with the staging key. That violates RFC 8414 §2 and needs no attacker — it is default behavior.

Worse, because the same constant is used on the verify side, staging is internally self-consistent while externally lying: it mints and validates the same false issuer, so ADR-018 Phase 1's "manual token-path exercise against staging" comes back GREEN while proving nothing about issuer identity. A production token also clears staging's issuer check, failing only on signature.

Nothing is confusable today (cloister's kid-resolver doesn't exist; signet's staticKeyProvider ignores issuerID) — but that is "the confusable path was never built", and ADR-018 tells a future integrator the opposite invariant holds.

FIX: move issuer to config, and move MINT (signing-authority.ts:574, :1040) and VERIFY (token.ts:133) together — changing only one side would make staging silently accept production tokens or vice versa. Related: notme-1532eb fixed the WIMSE trust domain the same way (derive from SITE_URL); this is the token-plane equivalent.

comments.text:
FIXED in PR #71 (commit 6d846df). The module constant is gone; `issuer` is now a REQUIRED parameter of both mintAccessToken and verifyAccessToken, with issuerFromEnv(env) deriving it from SIGNET_AUTHORITY_URL.

Making it required rather than defaulted is the load-bearing choice: the two DO mint sites (signing-authority.ts) were found by the type checker, not by searching. A third mint path — notme-bd2a72 proposes one — cannot silently inherit a hardcoded issuer.

Mint and verify moved together, per the bead: changing one side alone would have left staging accepting production tokens or the reverse. TDD proof is the cross-environment case — a production-issuer token is REJECTED when verified with the staging issuer, while the same token, same key, correct issuer is accepted, so the rejection is demonstrably the issuer check rather than something incidental. Two legacy tests asserting the hardcoded value now pass the issuer explicitly.

issuerFromEnv uses the same absent-vs-malformed discipline as wimseTrustDomain (notme-1532eb): absent → production default (the documented no-environment case); malformed → throws, because silently issuing production-issuer tokens from a misconfigured environment is precisely the defect being closed. Returns u.origin, so a trailing path or port oddity cannot produce a subtly different issuer string.

VERIFIED LIVE, which is what the AC asks for: staging redeployed (version 4c594952) and its discovery document now reports issuer https://auth-staging.notme.bot with token_endpoint https://auth-staging.notme.bot/token — previously it advertised the staging issuer while minting the production one. 495 unit + 95 real-DO green, staging 12/12.

Note for whoever closes ADR-018's Phase 1 gate: the "manual token-path exercise against staging" is now meaningful. Before this it was structurally incapable of detecting an issuer defect, since mint and verify shared the false constant.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: A token minted by the staging Worker carries iss matching its own discovery document's issuer, and staging rejects a token bearing the production issuer. Proven by a real-DO test driving both mint and verify with a non-production SIGNET_AUTHORITY_URL. cd worker && pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.workers.config.mts passes.

title: design: stop putting the /authorize access token in a URL (needs coordinated rig change)
description:
Split out of notme-07204f, which closes with PR #56. That bead's job was the FALSE CLAIM — THREAT_MODEL asserted the /authorize redirect token was DPoP-bound when it is an unbound bearer. That is fixed, corrected, and test-pinned. This bead carries the part that was NOT fixed: the exposure itself.

WHY IT IS A BEARER AT ALL (not a mistake). DPoP binds a token to a private key held in browser memory. That key does not survive the page navigation to redirect_uri — there is nothing left on the other side to prove possession with. `mintRedirectToken` (signing-authority.ts) omits `cnf.jkt` deliberately and says so. Every other notme path is proof-of-possession; this one cannot be, because a redirect cannot carry a key. Any fix has to change the DELIVERY, not the binding.

CURRENT EXPOSURE, verified at HEAD:
- worker.ts:926/933/937 — the /authorize page builds `${redirect_uri}?token=<access token>` and navigates to it.
- rig/web/src/index.ts:355 — the sole consumer reads it back with `c.req.query('token')`, a SERVER-SIDE query read (redirect issued at rig/web/src/index.ts:396 for /admin/setup-github).

Three unmitigated vectors:
1. Token in browser history on the user's machine.
2. Token in the destination's request line, therefore in Cloudflare's access logs for rig. LARGEST vector.
3. Onward Referer leakage from rig's page to third parties — governed by rig's Referrer-Policy, not notme's. Note the `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` added on the /authorize page does NOT address this; that was an overclaim corrected in PR #56 and it only protects the authorize URL's `state`.

SEVERITY: moderate, not critical. Bounded by a 5-minute lifetime; `aud` pins the token to ONE resource server so it is not a general-purpose credential; unique jti; it is an access token, not a session, so it cannot mint more; and /admin/setup-github is rarely exercised. Against that: an access token in a query parameter is what the OAuth 2.0 Security BCP tells you not to do, precisely because logs and history outlive the token's intended window.

OPTIONS, ranked. Every one breaks rig's server-side `c.req.query('token')` read, so every one is a coordinated two-repo change.

1. SINGLE-USE EXCHANGE CODE (RFC 6749 §4.1). /authorize redirects with `?code=<single-use, short-TTL>`; rig POSTs the code to notme and gets the token in a response body. The URL then carries no credential at all, and a logged code is worthless once redeemed. Correct long-term shape, and ADR-011 already lists `/oauth/authorize` + authorization-code exchange as missing — this would be a down payment on it rather than a detour. RECOMMENDED.
2. FRAGMENT (`#token=`). Fragments are never sent to a server and never appear in a Referer, so this kills vectors 2 and 3 outright and leaves only history. Cheapest real improvement. rig must move the read client-side (`location.hash`) and hand it over out-of-band.
3. POST-TO-TARGET (auto-submitting form). Token in a request body. Same rig-side change cost as (2) with no advantage over it.

Do not start until the option is chosen and the rig side is scheduled — a half-landed change breaks /admin/setup-github, which is itself the flow used to recover admin access.

title: Decide and record whether passkey registration to the CA is open to the internet
description:
Top remaining blocker from the Goal Zero identity audit (notme-c0a445). worker/worker.ts:839-849: only `isFirstUser` requires a bootstrap code. Everyone else registers a passkey freely, receives a session carrying bridgeCert, and exchanges it at /cert/passkey for a real CA-signed bridge cert pair. That is an open-registration certificate authority.

The comment at worker.ts:831 states it as intended ("Everyone else can register freely — gets bridgeCert scope only"), but the invite system (POST /invites → /join) exists and implies gating, and no ADR records a decision either way. Rate limiting (notme-191328) bounds the abuse rate; it does not answer the question.

This is a decision bead, not a defect bead: either gate registration behind an invite, or write down that open registration is intended, what it costs (anyone can obtain a bridgeCert-scoped cert chaining to the notme CA), and why that is acceptable. Shipping a CA whose registration policy exists only as an inline comment is deciding by omission.

Note the related divergence the same audit found: passkey users get session scopes from passkey_users.is_admin (worker.ts:876-878), never from capability_grants, so getCapabilities' revoked_at is inert for the primary user class — revoking a capability grant has no effect on a passkey user. Whatever registration policy is chosen should account for how those users are later de-authorized.

comments.text:
REFRAMED — this bead is not independently decidable, and the framing in its description is wrong. Raised by cloister (ADR-0028), verified against notme's code.

The open-registration question is DOWNSTREAM of a question notme has not asked: is this authority naming HUMANS or WORKLOADS? Filed as notme-600df1, which this bead now depends on.

The reason it cannot be answered on its own: "should registration be gated" has different answers depending on what registration establishes.
- If notme is a WORKLOAD authority, registration should be attested (what is running, where, from which build). Open registration is then obviously wrong AND passkey-as-the-gate is the wrong control entirely — so this bead's framing ("gate it behind an invite, or write down that open is intended") offers two answers that are both wrong.
- If notme is a HUMAN authority that bootstraps workload identity, passkey is exactly the right control, the 5-minute cert TTL is the correct mitigation, and open registration is survivable — but then the naming must change, because the principal is a human and the workload identity should be minted FROM it rather than AS it.

Cloister's own use is the second case (cloister-f2338f: a human at a laptop, one passkey touch, producing a short-lived cert a harness then uses unattended — notme as the human→machine bridge), and they argue notme is a human authority. They have standing in the answer: they consume notme as a workload-identity root (peerFp keys peer_attestations and the disclosure endpoint) while notme's strongest authentication is a human-presence control.

So the disposition changes from "decide open vs gated" to "decide the authority's kind first, then let the registration policy fall out". If the answer is human-authority, this bead likely resolves as "open registration is acceptable, with the conditions cloister named" — but resolving it that way BEFORE notme-600df1 would be recording a conclusion without its premise, which is how the original inline comment came to be the only statement of policy in the first place.

Keeping this open and blocked rather than closing it, since the registration decision still needs recording once the premise exists.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
Signet-side position on the registration-policy decision (from the signet Goal Zero release review, docs/release/goal-zero-promotion.md §4).

Signet's read: as implemented (worker.ts:839-849, bootstrap code required only for isFirstUser), this is an open-registration certificate authority — anyone can register a passkey and exchange the resulting session at /cert/passkey for a real CA-signed bridge cert pair. That is a defensible product decision for a public identity service, but it is not currently a DECISION anywhere; it is a default. The gap signet cares about is that the two are indistinguishable to a verifier.

Why this matters downstream of signet specifically: signet's verification pins the certificate identity and the issuing CA, not the enrollment policy. So a cert minted by a self-registered passkey is, to every signet verifier, exactly as valid as one minted for a trusted operator. If open registration is intended, then "chains to the notme CA" means "someone registered a passkey", and signet's docs must say that rather than implying vetting. If it is not intended, the bootstrap-code requirement should extend past the first user.

Signet's recommendation: whichever way it lands, record it as a normative statement in the ADR (what the CA asserts about a subject, and what it explicitly does not), because that sentence is what signet's verification docs will cite. Signet is content to wait on cloister's ADR — the user flagged this as correctly blocked there, and signet agrees the trust-domain semantics belong in that document rather than being decided ad hoc per repo.

Sequencing: not a gate on signet's v0.3.0 artifact release. It does constrain release-note language — signet will not describe the authority as closed-registration while this stands.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision (ADR or bead resolution) stating whether passkey registration is open or invite-gated, with the rationale and the de-authorization path for registered users; if gated, a test proves an un-invited registration is refused.

title: Verify against CF production whether Ed25519 SPKI import accepts a P-256 key
description:
Found 2026-08-04 while building /cert/passkey. Fixed forward in that PR; this bead is only about establishing the production blast radius, which I could not do from here.

THE BUG (fixed): `importPublicKey` (worker/src/cert-authority.ts) did "try Ed25519, fall back to ECDSA P-256 on throw". On workerd the Ed25519 import ACCEPTS a P-256 SPKI rather than throwing, so the fallback never ran and every key returned as `{name:"Ed25519"}`.

Reproduced in the vitest-pool-workers suite (real workerd):

    imported alg: {"name":"Ed25519"}     // from a P-256 SPKI
    spki roundtrip identical: true
    verify w/ ORIGINAL key: true
    verify w/ importPublicKey key: THREW —
      Requested algorithm "ECDSA" does not match this CryptoKey's algorithm "Ed25519"

CONSEQUENCE: the P-256 proof-of-possession check on every cert-issuing path — /cert/gha, /cert, /cert/passkey — threw and was caught as a 401. The certificate itself would have been fine (SPKI bytes round-trip intact); the failure is at PoP verification, and the 401 reads as "your proof is bad" when the proof is correct.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS FOR: I verified this against workerd as run by vitest-pool-workers. I did NOT verify Cloudflare's production build. Those can differ, and the difference decides whether this was a live production outage on /cert/gha (the primary CI identity path) or only ever affected local and CI.

Two readings, and they have very different implications:
- If prod behaves the same, /cert/gha has been rejecting valid GHA PoP proofs with 401 for as long as the try/catch has been there. That seems like something someone would have noticed, which is mild evidence AGAINST this reading.
- If prod's Ed25519 import correctly rejects a P-256 SPKI, the fallback worked there and the bug was confined to workerd-local and the CI suite.

HOW TO CHECK: exercise /cert/gha against the deployed worker with a real GHA OIDC token and real P-256 + Ed25519 ephemeral keys, and confirm a 200 rather than a 401 "P-256 proof-of-possession failed". The action already does exactly this — a green run of the GHA identity workflow against production, on a commit BEFORE the fix, answers it. `gh run list --workflow=gha-identity.yml` history may already contain the answer without running anything.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED, worth recording separately: `grep -rn importPublicKey src/__tests__` was EMPTY. Three call sites depended on it (cert-exchange.ts, cert-authority.ts, auth/derive-credentials.ts), each with its own coverage; the shared primitive underneath had none. Tests clustered at the level people reason about. src/import-public-key.do.test.ts now covers it.

Note derive-credentials.ts was unaffected in practice: it imports the CA public key, which IS Ed25519, so the wrong-algorithm import happened to be the right one.

comments.text:
CONFIRMED AGAINST PRODUCTION — this bead's question ("does it actually break in CF production?") is answered YES, and it is answered by deployment lag rather than by the code.

SIGNET REPORTED the live symptom: importPublicKey mis-detected signet's P-256 SPKI as Ed25519, so worker.ts verified an ECDSA proof against an Ed25519 key. Their diagnosis is correct and I verified both halves independently.

THE FIX IS IN MAIN. cert-authority.ts now dispatches on the SPKI algorithm OID (isEd25519Spki), landed in ddd5f98 (PR #64, [notme-7c7f83]), and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms it is an ancestor of origin/main. The code comment describes signet's exact symptom: an Ed25519 import of a P-256 SPKI SUCCEEDS rather than throwing, so the fallback never ran and every key came back as {name:'Ed25519'}.

THE PRODUCTION WORKER DOES NOT HAVE IT. Measured:
  production's live deployment: 2026-07-27T05:36Z (version 7d74131d)
  the fix landed:              2026-08-04T01:53
Production predates the fix by EIGHT DAYS and trails main by FORTY COMMITS.

So this is not an outstanding code defect — it is an outstanding DEPLOYMENT. Signet stays broken until production is redeployed, and no amount of further work in this repo changes that.

OTHER EVIDENCE OF THE SAME LAG, consistent with the dates: production's JWKS reports an 8-character kid while staging reports 32, so production also predates the canonical-128-bit-kid fix. And every unmatched path under auth.notme.bot returns 500/1101 (notme-cb0354), which the fix for is on goalzero.

DEPLOY SAFETY, checked so the decision is not made blind: no new [[migrations]] entries exist between the deployed version and main — the declared tags are still v1 and v2. So a version of MAIN can be split-deployed via the canary path (`task ship`, `worker:canary NEW= OLD= PCT=`, `worker:promote`), and rollback is promoting the old version id. The DO-migration hazard that would force an atomic promote does not apply here.

RECOMMENDATION, and the distinction matters: deploy MAIN, not goalzero. Main already contains this fix and unblocks signet; goalzero carries 60+ commits with six open Goal Zero blockers and should still go through its own gate. Treating "signet is broken" as a reason to ship unreviewed work would be exactly the coupling ADR-018 exists to prevent.

This bead stays open pending that deploy, and its disposition on notme-c0a37e was already "LINKED to a concrete prerequisite" — the prerequisite is now identified precisely: a production deployment of main.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
PRODUCTION DEPLOYED — the prerequisite this bead was linked to is now satisfied. signet should re-test.

Deployed main (NOT goalzero, which still carries six open Goal Zero blockers) through the canary path: version 39e0b216 uploaded carrying no traffic, split 10/90 against the prior 7d74131d, verified, then promoted to 100% at 2026-08-06T02:21Z. Post-promotion `task worker:verify` green, 12/12.

WHAT THIS FIXES for signet: the deployed Worker now contains ddd5f98 (PR #64), so importPublicKey dispatches on the SPKI algorithm OID instead of mis-detecting a P-256 SPKI as Ed25519. Production had been running code from 2026-07-27, eight days older than the fix and forty commits behind main.

RIDING ALONG, worth knowing since it changes production behaviour beyond this bead: the promoted version binds TOKEN_LIMITER (20/60s), CERT_LIMITER (10/60s) and PASSKEY_LIMITER (5/60s) for the first time. Production had been running with all three unbound — every limiter a silent no-op — because the blocks existed only in wrangler.toml.example (notme-191328). Passkey registration, /token and cert exchange are now rate-limited in production. If signet's flows see unexpected 429s, that is why, and the limits are tunable.

STILL NOT FIXED IN PRODUCTION, because the fix lives on goalzero rather than main: unmatched paths under auth.notme.bot still return 500/error 1101 (notme-cb0354). Re-confirmed just now. That is not a regression from this deploy — it predates it — but it means a signet request to a path notme does not route will surface as a server error rather than a 404.

ASK FOR SIGNET: re-run the failing enrollment and confirm. If it still fails, the diagnosis was incomplete rather than the deployment stale, and I would want the exact request/response rather than the symptom.

Leaving this bead OPEN until signet confirms — the AC is about verifying the behaviour against CF production, and only signet can close that loop.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
CONFIRMED BY SIGNET, closing. Their evidence is stronger than a passing check: the ECDSA verify could not have executed at all unless `importPublicKey` had dispatched correctly on the SPKI algorithm OID. So version 39e0b216 was live and working as of 2026-08-06T02:29Z, on evidence that could not have appeared otherwise — a positive that is only producible by the fixed code path, rather than an absence of errors.

Worth noting what that same run then found, because it is the reason this bead closes and another opens: reaching the ECDSA verify at all is what EXPOSED the second bug behind it (notme-a011d2, PoP double-hashing). The P-256 SPKI break was masking it. Fixed and deployed since — production is now 91b54069, worker:verify 13/13.

title: Canonical CBOR multi-key fixture exercises the branch production never takes
description:
From the type-correctness review (goal notme-cf288e). sortStringKeysCanonical (worker/src/revocation.ts:183-196) has a length comparison followed by a bytewise tiebreak. The only multi-key fixture, schema/fixtures/cabundle-multikey, uses {"ab","b"} — which returns on the LENGTH branch.

Real kids are lowercasehex(SHA-256(SPKI)[:16]) per worker/src/key-id.ts, so they are ALWAYS exactly 32 characters. Production therefore always takes the bytewise tiebreak branch, which nothing tests, and never takes the branch that is tested.

Multi-key bundles occur during key rotation — precisely when a cross-implementation divergence between notme, signet and ley-line-open would be worst to diagnose.

Tempering (the reviewer's own): for equal-length ASCII hex, canonical and plain-alphabetical ordering coincide, so most plausible mis-implementations would still agree on real data. This is coverage of the branch that matters, not a known divergence.

Fix: add schema/fixtures/cabundle-rotation — two realistic 32-hex-char kids listed in reversed JSON order (so a pass can only come from sorting), a realistic 32-byte key value, a present prevKeyId, and a realistic uint32 issuedAt. Note the related gap the identity audit found: no fixture has prevKeyId PRESENT, and prevKeyId !== "" together with keys.length > 1 is exactly the rotation-grace state generateBundle produces — so one fixture closes both.
acceptance_criteria: schema/fixtures/ contains a rotation fixture with two equal-length 32-hex kids in non-canonical JSON order and a present prevKeyId; bundle-canonical.test.ts consumes it; the test fails if sortStringKeysCanonical's bytewise tiebreak is broken. cd worker && pnpm exec vitest run src/__tests__/bundle-canonical.test.ts passes.

title: Canary soak verify samples traffic instead of targeting the new version — a broken canary passes ~90% of the time
description:
From the type-correctness review of ADR-018 (goal notme-cf288e). At the documented PCT=10 canary split, a `task worker:verify` run has roughly a 90% chance of measuring the OLD version, so a broken NEW version passes any single check about nine times in ten.

ADR-018 discloses the ambiguity honestly ("verify green during soak — may hit either version, both must hold the contract"), which is why this is not a blocker: the stated exit criterion is technically satisfiable by either version holding the contract. But it READS as evidence about NEW, and an operator promoting on it believes they tested the new version.

Fix: Cloudflare gradual deployments support a version-override request header (`Cloudflare-Workers-Version-Overrides`, spelling to be confirmed against current CF docs) that pins a request to a specific version id. Teaching `worker:verify` an optional VERSION= that sets it would turn the soak check into real evidence about NEW specifically, and the canary exit criterion could then require a green run pinned to the new version id rather than a sampled one.

Until then ADR-018's Phase 2 exit criteria should say plainly that verify during soak is a sampled check, not proof about the new version — the honest disclosure is already there, but the criterion above it is not worded to match.

comments.text:
CONFIRMED IN A REAL PRODUCTION CANARY, and it is worse than this bead estimated — plus the fix is already available and works.

During the 2026-08-06 production promotion of main (version 39e0b216 at 10%, prior 7d74131d at 90%, split confirmed active by `wrangler deployments list`), I sampled the authority 85 times with distinct cache-busting queries. ALL 85 responses came from the OLD version. At a 10% split the probability of that by chance is 0.9^85 ≈ 0.01%.

So this bead's framing — "a verify run has roughly a 90% chance of measuring OLD" — understates it. From a single client the canary may be effectively invisible: not 90/10 sampling, but 100/0. `task worker:verify` during a soak is therefore not weak evidence about the new version, it is potentially NO evidence.

Ruled out as explanations: the Cache API is not masking it (cacheKey preserves the query string, so distinct queries are distinct entries and each request reached the Worker), and the split was genuinely live per Cloudflare's own deployment listing.

THE FIX THIS BEAD PROPOSES WORKS — I used it to complete the promotion safely. The header is:
  Cloudflare-Workers-Version-Overrides: notme-bot="<version-id>"
Sending it pins the request to a specific version. I ran all twelve contract checks pinned to 39e0b216 BEFORE promoting; all twelve passed, which is direct evidence about the new version rather than sampled evidence about whichever version answered.

A TRAP WORTH RECORDING, because it nearly produced a false pass. I first tried to distinguish versions by a code-derived signal — the JWKS `kid`, which main computes as 128-bit/32-hex while the deployed version predated that change. Pinned to the NEW version the kid was still 8 hex. The reason: the kid is STORED STATE in the Durable Object, written when the key was created, not recomputed per request. A code change to the derivation does not alter an existing key's stored kid.

The general lesson for whoever implements this: a canary's distinguishing signal MUST be derived from the code path under test, not read from persisted state — otherwise the check passes identically on both versions and tells you nothing. Pinning is what caught it; sampling would have "confirmed" the new version was fine on evidence that could not have shown otherwise.

RAISING PRIORITY IS WARRANTED. ADR-018's Phase 2 exit criterion currently reads as evidence about NEW and, as measured here, may be evidence about nothing. Until the VERSION= parameter lands, the honest procedure is: pin with the override header before promoting, and treat the unpinned soak run as a service-health check only.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: `task worker:verify VERSION=<id>` pins requests to that version via the CF version-override header and is proven to reach it (e.g. a check that fails against a known-different version); ADR-018 Phase 2 exit criteria reference the pinned run.

title: cross-repo: cloister state re-survey before any operadic-substrate composition design lands
description:
User flagged at end of 010-workerd-as-rope conversation (2026-04-28/29) that **cloister has changed substantially** since the conversation that generated `ley-line-3278b4` (substrate ADR) and `notme-e005a8` (mTLS-injector chunk-spec). The math-friend's load-bearing recommendation: re-survey cloister BEFORE writing any cross-repo composition design.

Filed in notme because cloister has no `.beads/` directory; tracking from the consumer side.

## What to do

Fresh seam-discovery pass on cloister. Use the `seam-discovery` skill. Answer:

1. **Current shape.** Cloister at `~/remotes/art/cloister`. What does its src/, manifest/, capnp surfaces look like as of today (commit hash + last-touched dates)? It currently has: `cloister.capnp`, `config.capnp`, `src/`, `manifest/`, melange/apko packaging.
2. **Capabilities exposed.** What does cloister currently expose to consumers? What runtime contracts? Where is the seam to ley-line / workerd / notme?
3. **Relationship to workerd.** Math-friend flagged this specifically. Is cloister still the planned host for content-addressed isolate composition, or has its scope drifted?
4. **What's parked there.** The `notme-e005a8` description says "ley-line substrate ADR (currently parked in cloister as `[destined for ley-line]` until ley-line's `.beads/dolt` schema migration completes)" — verify whether that parking is still in place or has moved.
5. **Math-friend's critique exposure.** Does cloister's current shape change which of the 5 falsifiable predictions in `ley-line-3278b4` are easy/hard to test?

## Why this blocks the substrate ADR

Bead `ley-line-3278b4` (substrate ADR) is the cross-repo design pivot. If cloister has drifted substantially since the conversation, the substrate ADR risks being written against a phantom — math-friend specifically flagged this as a load-bearing call.

## Artifacts

- Output: short markdown survey at `notme/docs/design/cloister-survey-$(date).md` (or wherever appropriate). Include: current cloister architecture diagram, list of contracts/capabilities, identified seams to ley-line + notme + workerd, list of any parked-here-but-destined-elsewhere material.
- Comment back here with the survey path + any deltas from the picture in `notme/docs/design/010-handoff.md`.

## Blocks

- `ley-line-3278b4` (substrate ADR) — should not land without this survey first.

title: POC: load tree-root hash → instantiate notme-proxy + tiny HTTP echo Worker as a unit (math-friend's smallest viable end-to-end)
description:
Math-friend's recommended smallest-viable POC for the operadic-Merkle-DAG substrate (`ley-line-3278b4`). End-to-end before any schema decisions land. If it works, the rest is fleshing out the picture; if it doesn't, the whole frame needs rethinking.

## What to build

- Existing notme-proxy (Rust, holds in-memory mTLS key — never extracted, never shared).
- 50-line HTTP echo Worker (workerd-runnable; trivial).
- Hash both as chunks per the substrate ADR's chunk schema.
- 200-line Rust loader that takes a single tree-root hash and instantiates them as a unit.
- Verify: HTTP request through the loader → echo Worker sees mTLS-attached request from notme-proxy.

## Why it matters

This is the empirical falsifier for the entire substrate frame. Either the loader-from-tree-root model produces a working composed deployment OR it doesn't. No amount of ADR refinement substitutes for this measurement.

## DO NOT START until

- `ley-line-3278b4` (substrate ADR) has answers — chunk schema, capability resolution, identity model picked.
- `notme-32c72f` (cloister re-survey) is done — POC may need to consume cloister output, depending on what re-survey reveals.

If you start before those answers, you'll bake in arbitrary choices the substrate ADR is supposed to derive.

## Hard constraint (architectural decision 2026-04-29)

notme-proxy stays where it is, NOT extracted to a generic `cloister-companion`. The mTLS key lives in notme-proxy memory and never appears in any chunk content. The chunk is a *manifest* describing how a deployment binds notme-proxy as a capability; the key crosses no chunk boundary.

## Acceptance

- HTTP echo Worker receives a request bearing the mTLS identity from notme-proxy.
- The composed unit is loadable from a single tree-root hash.
- Loader is ≤300 LOC of Rust (math-friend's 200-LOC target + 50% slack).
- Spike branch only — DO NOT merge the loader into a notme/ley-line crate without ADR sign-off.

title: Emit artifact-only server.json via leyline-mcp-descriptor v0.13.0
description:
LLO v0.13.0 shipped everything this was waiting on; the emit side is unblocked TODAY (full brief: ley-line-open/_agent_log/2026-07-30-for-notme.md).

- Binary: leyline-mcp-descriptor-{linux,darwin}-{amd64,arm64} in the v0.13.0 release assets, SHA256SUMS-verified.
- Shape: packages[] OMITTED entirely (never a placeholder transport); _meta.'io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided'.artifacts = [{registryType:'oci', identifier:'ghcr.io/agentic-research/notme' (TAGLESS), version:'<tag>'}, {…notme-proxy…}]. Artifact entries pass the same tagless-identifier + version validation as packages entries.
- The rendered notme-shaped example is already the contract fixture on cloister-02dd65 — emit exactly that.
- Wire regeneration into notme's release flow with a stale-check (LLO's gen:server-json:check pattern) so a version bump can't leave the descriptor behind.
- Caveat, stated so it isn't discovered the hard way: cloister's CONSUMER (cloister-02dd65) is still open — end-to-end OCI-pin derivation validates when they land. Emitting now is safe; the shape cannot drift without breaking LLO's own generated conformance.

comments.text:
DONE. server.json is now artifact-only and, for the first time, actually
validated against the schema it declares.

## Verified before writing anything

- v0.13.0 release exists; `leyline-mcp-descriptor-darwin-arm64` downloaded and
  checksum-matched against the release `SHA256SUMS`
  (`b5e9c49fbbcc7a08…6fe609`).
- The shape is legal, from the schema rather than from the brief:
  `ServerDetail.required` is `["name","description","version"]` — `packages` is
  NOT required — and
  `_meta."io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided"` is declared
  `additionalProperties: true`, so `artifacts` is a sanctioned occupant.
- `Package.required` really is `["registryType","identifier","transport"]`,
  confirming notme-6e5330's finding at the source.

## The artifacts block matches the emitter, proven not assumed

Fed a notme descriptor to the v0.13.0 binary and diffed its rendered
publisher-provided block against the committed file:

    diff <(jq -S '._meta["io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided"]' llo-rendered.json) \
         <(jq -S '._meta["io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided"]' server.json)
    -> IDENTICAL

## Hand-maintained, not generated — with a measured reason

Running the emitter showed exactly what a generated file would cost. Its
output has no `title`, no `websiteUrl`, and `_meta` is a closed two-field
struct (`art.cloister/v1` for tool-group claims, `publisher-provided`).
Adopting it wholesale would drop five things:

  1. `title`
  2. `websiteUrl`
  3. `_meta."io.github.agentic-research.notme/surface"`
  4. `_meta."io.github.agentic-research.notme/packages"`
  5. `_meta."art.cloister/v1".bundles[]` — the notme-identity / notme-proxy
     hypervisor-tier topology (ADR-0011/0018/0005), ~40 lines that are notme's
     own and not derivable from an image address

(5) is the sharp one: the crate puts TOOL-GROUP claims under that same
`art.cloister/v1` key, and omits the key entirely when there are no groups.
notme has no groups, so a generated file silently drops the block rather than
colliding with it. The input shape is also documented upstream as "This input
shape WILL change."

So: the file stays hand-maintained and matches the emitter where the contract
lives (the artifacts array). This is answer (b) on notme-450c3c's acceptance
criteria — adoption rejected on measured evidence, with the reason recorded in
the file's own `_meta`.

## The drift check the bead asked for, in two halves

`task server:check` (new, wired into ci.yml's `check` job) and
`task version:check VERSION=<tag>` (existing, runs before every publish).
Neither subsumes the other: nothing on a branch knows the release tag, so the
PR gate can't assert it — and running ONLY the release gate is precisely how
both known defects reached main. `--self` says so in its own success output
instead of implying it checked a tag it never saw.

New assertions, each falsification-tested by mutating the file and confirming
a non-zero exit:

  - schema conformance via ajv against a VENDORED, sha256-pinned copy of the
    2025-12-11 schema (`schema/mcp/server.schema.2025-12-11.json`, byte-identical
    to both the canonical URL and LLO's copy — 3fba0959…14de0)
  - `packages` key refused outright (regression gate — the old shape can only
    come back as a schema violation or a fabricated transport)
  - top-level `version` must agree too
  - artifacts entries keep BOTH halves of ADR-0041 §2: absent version fatal,
    tagged identifier fatal, checked per-entry with exact tag-stripped matching

## It found a second, unknown defect on its first run

`/description: must NOT have more than 100 characters` — the description was
135. Unrelated to the transport bug, never checked by anything, and it would
have been rejected by any registry validating on ingest. Shortened to 87.

That is the argument for the PR gate in one line: notme-6e5330 was found by
another repo, and this one was found by the check, not by us.

## Not yet end-to-end

cloister-02dd65 (the consumer that derives OCI pins from this extension) is
still open — verified, not taken from the brief. Emitting now is safe and the
shape cannot drift without breaking LLO's own generated conformance, but the
full derive path lights up only when that lands.

Files: server.json, scripts/check-image-versions.ts,
schema/mcp/server.schema.2025-12-11.json, Taskfile.yml,
.github/workflows/ci.yml, .gitignore, packages/README.md, scripts/README.md
(the bead's `files` said only package.json, which was wrong — noting it so a
future dispatch scopes correctly).

title: notme: GitHub Actions disabled at repo level — 7 open PRs have no CI signal
description:
Discovered while checking why PR #2-#8 (opened in this session) have no CI status. The workflow file at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` looks fine and lists as "active" via `gh workflow list`, but `gh api repos/agentic-research/notme/actions/permissions` returns:

```json
{"enabled":false,"sha_pinning_required":false}
```

That's an org/repo-level kill switch. Workflows can't fire while it's set. Confirms why:
- "Test Identity Exchange" workflow only ran via `workflow_dispatch` (manual trigger that sometimes ignores the disable, depending on org policy)
- CI workflow has `total_count: 0` historical runs since 7aa843d added it 4 weeks ago
- All 7 of this session's PRs (PR #2 through #8) have empty `statusCheckRollup`

**Fix:** enable Actions on the repo. UI path: Settings → Actions → General → "Allow all actions and reusable workflows" (or your preferred policy). API path:
```
gh api -X PUT repos/agentic-research/notme/actions/permissions \
  --input - <<<'{"enabled":true,"allowed_actions":"all"}'
```

Once enabled, push/PR triggers fire and CI signal returns. The 7 open PRs would re-run by closing+reopening or pushing an empty commit.

**Why it was disabled is the operator question** — possibly turned off during the security audit work (rosary-b22de6 hardening pass) or org-level cost control. Re-enabling needs explicit operator decision.

This is the operator action; an agent shouldn't flip the kill switch.

Side note: even with this disabled, I've been verifying tsc + vitest locally on every commit — but external CI would catch environmental drift (Node version, lockfile mismatch, etc.) that local doesn't.

title: Conform notme-proxy's MCP surface to the sessionless 2026-07-28 protocol pin
description:
LLO pinned the MCP wire schema: vendored protocol.2026-07-28.json, digest ef70b61f99b6d2e5e3b46863822eab08dff6a45bedc7a08914e0e5b133f40203, gated at COMPILE time on the LLO side. The pinned protocol is sessionless — no initialize (SEP-2567/2575 removed sessions) and no ping. If notme-proxy speaks MCP (either direction):

1. Remove/refuse initialize and ping rather than tolerating them — LLO's daemon refuses them with a do-not-extend posture (LLO bead 1227f2 tracks the daemon handshake hardening).
2. Add a conformance test that fetches or vendors the SAME protocol.2026-07-28.json and asserts its digest, so drift on either side fails a test rather than an integration.
3. Method names should come from the schema (LLO generates METHOD_* consts from $defs[].properties.method.const — same technique works in TS).

Reference: ley-line-open/rs/ll-core/mcp-protocol-schema/ and ley-line-open/_agent_log/2026-07-30-for-notme.md.

comments.text:
NO-OP — notme-proxy has no MCP surface to conform. Verified 2026-07-30, not assumed.

The bead is correctly conditional ("If notme-proxy speaks MCP (either
direction)"). It does not, in either direction:

    $ grep -rniE 'jsonrpc|\bmcp\b|initialize|tools/list' proxy/
    proxy/README.md:20:        agent["agent / CLI / MCP"]

One hit, in a mermaid node label naming the *client* upstream of the proxy.
`proxy/src/main.rs` is 1031 lines and its whole surface is transport:
`parse_listen_addr`, `load_certs_and_key`, `build_mtls_config`,
`validate_uds_path`, `proxy_to_uds`, `handle_uds`, `dispatch`, `handle_proxy`.
No JSON-RPC dependency in `proxy/Cargo.toml` — no serde_json, no jsonrpc crate.
The UDS path, per the module docstring, "writes the request body verbatim,
half-closes, reads bytes-back, returns them in a 200."

So the proxy CARRIES MCP bytes and never parses them. There is no `initialize`
to remove because there is nothing that could send or recognise one, and no
method-name table to generate from `$defs[].properties.method.const` because
no method names appear in the code.

## The pin is worth knowing anyway — it confirms the design

The 2026-07-28 schema being SESSIONLESS (SEP-2567/2575 removed sessions) is
load-bearing news for this proxy in the opposite direction from the bead's
framing. The UDS mode is strictly one-shot: write body → half-close → read
bytes → 200. A sessionful protocol requiring a persistent stream across an
`initialize` handshake could NOT be carried over that shape. Sessionless can.

The pin therefore validates the existing transport rather than requiring a
change to it. Worth recording because the reverse — MCP re-growing sessions —
WOULD be a real break here, and it would break at the transport layer where
nothing currently looks for it.

## Recommend

Close as no-op. Item 2 (a conformance test pinning LLO's schema digest) is not
worth adding: a digest assertion over a schema nothing in this repo reads
tests only that a file was downloaded. Refile if notme ever grows an MCP
surface — at which point `_meta` in server.json must move from `artifacts`
back to `packages[]` WITH a real transport, and that is the moment the pin
starts to bite.

Cross-ref: notme-38044e (artifact-only server.json, landed) records the same
"notme serves no MCP" fact in the file cloister actually reads.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: proxy neither sends nor accepts initialize/ping; conformance test pins the same schema digest LLO gates compilation on

title: schema-bridge: handle Go-annotation declarations so task gen:zod runs on notme/schema/identity.capnp
description:
**Re-filed from rosary-8d2c78** (reconciler-busted; re-filed in target repo).

Surfaced during B.3 (schema-bridge lift in PR #21 — merged).

# Issue
`task gen:zod` against `notme/schema/identity.capnp` errors with `unmapped capnp construct annotation at node id=bea97f1023792be0`. Root cause: `identity.capnp` uses `$Go.package`/`$Go.import` for the existing `schema:go` task; capnp emits the imported `/go.capnp`'s annotation **declarations** as `Node.Annotation` nodes, which schema-bridge rejects at `packages/schema-bridge/src/inputs/capnp.rs:128-130`. Zero impact on zod output (the annotations describe Go codegen) but trips schema-bridge's fail-fast policy.

# Three fix options (recommend option 2)

**Option 1**: Allow ALL annotation declarations to be skipped (loosens the fail-fast policy across the board — fragile).

**Option 2 (RECOMMENDED)**: Allowlist the Go annotation file id `@0xd12a1c51fedd6c88` alongside the existing `ANN_JSON_*` constants in `packages/schema-bridge/src/inputs/capnp.rs`. Surgical, preserves fail-fast for everything else.

**Option 3**: Strip Go annotations from notme/schema/identity.capnp at codegen time (preprocessor). Doesn't scale to other annotation systems.

# Done when
- `task gen:zod` succeeds against notme/schema/identity.capnp
- Committed baseline `notme/gen/ts/identity.zod.ts`
- `task gen:zod:check-drift` works as designed

# Depends on
- nothing (PR #21 already landed schema-bridge in notme/packages/)

title: ADR hygiene: extend @doc-check to ADRs 005-012, resolve duplicate numbers, backfill Status lines
description:
Full ADR-vs-code audit run 2026-08-04. Findings, and what is left after the mechanical fixes already applied.

## The systemic issue

`task docs:check` reports "All 35 claims verified" and is green. It covers 5 of 14 design docs — only those carrying the @doc-check annotation: 006, 013, 014, 015, 016. ADRs 005, 007 (x2), 008, 009, 010, 011, 012 (x2) are entirely unverified prose.

That is not a coincidence in where drift was found: every stale claim in this audit was in an uncovered doc. The gate reads as comprehensive while covering the recent minority, and nothing in its output says otherwise. It should report coverage (docs checked / docs total), and every design doc should either carry @doc-check or an explicit opt-out with a reason.

## Fixed in this pass (branch notme-as-metadata-pkce-comment)

- ADR-011 gap table listed /oauth/authorize, PKCE, and code->token exchange as missing. ADR-013 shipped all three. Third instance of this rot in the same file family.
- ADR-011 Bead line said "(TBD - bd embeddeddolt format mismatch)". notme-0078a9 was filed 2026-06-25 and scopes docs/design/011-external-oauth-provider.md.
- 007-secretless-local-proxy, 007-secretless-plan, 008, 009 had NO Status line. Backfilled with audited status.
- as-metadata.ts: two comments and one published value justified by claims ADR-013 falsified (see sibling commits).

## Remaining work

1. **@doc-check coverage** — extend to 005, 007 x2, 008, 009, 010, 011, 012 x2, or record why a doc is exempt. Make the gate print coverage.
2. **Duplicate ADR numbers.** Two 007s (007-secretless-local-proxy = the decision, 007-secretless-plan = the plan) and two 012s (012-sender-constrained-oidc, Proposed; 012-vault-retirement, Accepted). Not renumbered here on purpose: cloister and other repos link to these paths, so renumbering is a cross-repo change and the user's call. Cheapest fix is probably renumbering the Proposed 012 to the next free number, since nothing depends on a Proposed ADR.
3. **012-sender-constrained-oidc has no bead** — its Bead line says "file when rsry reaches notme", which has long since happened.
4. **ADR-006 cites notme.bot-2b0d41** — a pre-rename repo prefix that resolves to nothing under either prefix. Either remap or drop.
5. **ADR-016 has no Bead line.** It generalizes 014/015 and was prompted by cloister review; may legitimately have no bead, but should say so rather than omit the field.

## Verification caveat worth recording

.beads/beads.jsonl is a STALE export. An initial pass over it flagged notme-7c7f83 (ADR-005) and notme-2bba44 (ADR-013) as dangling; both resolve fine against the live Dolt store — 7c7f83 is done, 2bba44 is legitimately open pending the rig change. Any ADR-to-bead reconciliation must query the live store, not the jsonl. This is the same lag that made scripts/bead-ref-check.ts warn rather than fail.

## Genuine code-vs-doc gap found

007-secretless-local-proxy's headline claim is STILL TRUE for the CF edge deployment: signing-authority.ts exports the CA private JWK and JSON.stringify's it into DO SQLite in persistent mode. Ephemeral (workerd) mode is fixed with extractable:false. The doc having no Status line meant nothing indicated whether this was solved. Tracked by notme-ae3130.
acceptance_criteria: `task docs:check` reports coverage (docs checked / docs total) rather than a bare claim count, and every docs/design/*.md either carries @doc-check or an explicit opt-out reason. Duplicate ADR numbers 007 and 012 resolved. No ADR lacks a Status line.

title: CA master + delegated JWT private keys are plaintext JWK in DO SQLite, while cloister's vault envelope-encrypts — root weaker than leaves
description:
Found while checking whether the ADR audit misaligns with cloister/vault after the ADR-012 vault lift. It does, and the direction is the wrong one.

## The asymmetry

cloister/vault (ADR-0030 §A3, lifted OUT of notme) does full envelope encryption:
- KEK derived from a Worker secret via HKDF (vault/src/kek-source.ts)
- random per-encrypt AES-256-GCM DEK; KEK wraps the DEK (vault/src/crypto.ts)
- sealed blob = {wrappedDek, iv, ciphertext}
- three-tier scoping with per-tenant HKDF info string "cloister/cred-iso/v1/tenant/<name>", so different tenantName means independent KEK (vault/src/kek-scope.ts)

notme's SigningAuthority DO does none of it:

    CREATE TABLE keys (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, private_jwk TEXT NOT NULL, ...)
    INSERT INTO keys (...) VALUES ('authority', JSON.stringify(privateJwk), ...)

The CA master Ed25519 private key is stored as a plaintext JWK. grep confirms nothing encrypts private_jwk anywhere in worker/src.

## Blast radius is inverted

- cloister vault compromise: tenant credentials, header values. Bad, scoped, per-tenant KEKs limit it.
- notme CA master key compromise: mint a cert for ANY identity with ANY scopes; forge at+jwt access tokens that every notme resource server accepts (ADR-015 records that verifyAccessToken leaves issuer unchecked by default); sign CA bundles; sign Interlace receipts.

The substrate encrypted the leaves and left the root in the clear. The key with the largest blast radius has the weakest storage.

## notme's own stated standard fails

007-secretless-local-proxy: "A system that claims to be secretless cannot have `cat *.sqlite | strings | grep '\"d\"'` extract the CA key." That is exactly the current persistent-mode state.

## It is a KNOWN unimplemented design, not an oversight

platform.ts validateKeyStorageConfig throws for mode "encrypted": "encrypted key storage is not yet implemented ... Fail hard so operators don't get a false sense of security." Failing closed is the right call and deserves credit — but it means production runs cf-managed with the key in cleartext.

## ADR-015 inherited it

delegated_jwt_keys (issuer, private_jwk TEXT NOT NULL, ...) — the per-issuer delegated signing keys added for ADR-015 in this same session go into the same plaintext table. The separate-key control that ADR-015 relies on still holds cryptographically (a delegated token cannot verify against notme's JWKS), but at-rest both keys are equally exposed.

## Why this is now cheap

Two working implementations of the exact pattern already exist in the org:
- cloister/vault/src/crypto.ts + kek-source.ts — the envelope + KEK rails, same runtime (Workers + DO + Web Crypto)
- notme's own worker/src/auth/dpop-nonce.ts — HKDF key derivation from a Worker secret under a domain separator, shipped and tested

So this is wiring an established in-org pattern into signing-authority.ts, not new crypto design.

## Threat-model caveat, stated honestly

The `cat *.sqlite` attack is most direct against local/workerd, and that path is ALREADY fixed — ephemeral mode uses extractable:false and stores an empty private_jwk. On the CF edge, DO SQLite is CF-managed and an attacker with Worker execution could sign regardless. What envelope encryption buys is separating "can read DO storage" from "can read Worker secrets" — two different compromise surfaces. That separation is precisely what cloister judged worth building, and notme holds the more valuable key.

Related: notme-ae3130 (007 Platform interface differs from implementation) is about the interface, not key-at-rest — different bead.

comments.text:
Implemented in `d35bf79` on branch `notme-as-metadata-pkce-comment` (PR #66). 557 tests pass (475 unit + 82 workers).

**Licensing — the part worth recording.** The obvious move was to copy `cloister/vault/src/crypto.ts`. That file is **AGPL-3.0-or-later**; notme is Apache-2.0, so copying it back would have pulled AGPL into an Apache-2.0 repo. cloister's own `vault/NOTICE` anticipates this: *"the original copy in notme remains under Apache 2.0 and is unaffected."* So `src/key-encryption.ts` is built on notme's own Apache-2.0 `vault/src/crypto.ts`, recovered from git history (deleted in `0d3ec86`, ADR-012). Verified the two files are byte-identical apart from their three-line license headers — cloister has not hardened it since the documented 2026-05-17 re-incorporation, so nothing was lost by taking the Apache side. The `cloister-9ad9eb` / `notme-9af5dd` divergence plan currently has zero divergence to manage.

**What shipped**

- Domain-separated KEK — salt `notme-authority-kek-v1`, info `signing-key-encryption`, deliberately different from the vault's. One operator secret may plausibly be reused across both subsystems; matching parameters would let a vault blob unseal under the authority KEK. There is a test for this.
- Covers the CA master **and** `delegated_jwt_keys`. ADR-015 added that table into the plaintext posture it inherited.
- Migration: sealed and legacy rows coexist, discriminated on an explicit marker rather than the absence of JWK fields. Master re-seals in place on first read. A sealed row met with no KEK **throws** rather than falling through to key generation — that fall-through would silently invalidate every cert and token ever issued.
- `platform.ts` had two unconditional throws for encrypted mode while `detectKeyStorage` auto-selects it when `NOTME_KEK_SECRET` is set. Setting the secret bricked the authority on boot. Now fails closed only on encrypted-with-no-secret.

**Acceptance criteria** — `key-encryption.test.ts` asserts the stored column contains neither the `d` value, nor the literal `"d"`, nor the plaintext JWK JSON. Plus tamper rejection, wrong-KEK rejection, empty-secret refusal, and both migration directions.

**Bonus finding, and the reason the user pushed back mid-implementation.** `#getKek` was first written as TS `private` and `rpc-surface.do.test.ts` caught it as method 47 against a pin of 46. Auditing for the same pattern found **five more** already-live leaks: `ensureSchema`, `getKeyId`, `keyStorageMode`, `ensureAlarmHealthSchema`, `readAlarmHealthRow`. TS `private` is erased at compile time — it hides a member from the author and from nobody else. All converted to ECMAScript `#private`; surface pin 46 → 41. None was individually dangerous, but the pin had been blessing them. Recorded as a standing rule so it stops recurring.

**Still plaintext by design:** `cf-managed` with no `NOTME_KEK_SECRET` set. That is the deliberate opt-out relying on Cloudflare's encryption at rest. Setting the secret on an existing deployment migrates the key on next read.

Not closing until PR #66 merges.

Cross-repo follow-up filed: **cloister-6ea153** — extract the AES-GCM envelope primitive to a permissive npm package.

This bead's implementation created a third copy of that code. Rather than copy cloister's AGPL `vault/src/crypto.ts` into Apache-2.0 notme, it was rebuilt from notme's own Apache-2.0 original recovered from git history — correct, but archaeology, and the second time it has been needed.

The licence direction is the blocker — AGPL can consume permissive, not the reverse, so the shared package must be permissive or notme can never depend on it.

Scope swept across cloister, notme, rosary, mache, ley-line, ley-line-open, rig, assay and signet: only cloister and notme carry this code. Nothing else in the ecosystem is affected.

Nothing here is blocked — notme's copy is Apache-2.0 and clean, so this release ships as-is.

comments.text:
Signet-side position on the key-custody decision (from the signet Goal Zero release review, docs/release/goal-zero-promotion.md §4).

Signet's read: the asymmetry is the finding. Signet's entire trust story is that the CA is the root — bridge certs, the release-signing enrollment path (/cert/gha), and the CA bundle every verifier fetches from /.well-known/ca-bundle.pem all chain to it. Plaintext JWK for the CA master while cloister's vault envelope-encrypts the leaves inverts the protection gradient: the key whose compromise is unrecoverable is the least protected one. Leaf compromise expires in five minutes; CA compromise invalidates every artifact ever signed, including releases already in the wild that verifiers will keep validating against that anchor indefinitely (signet's release verification deliberately re-fetches the live anchor — see scripts/release/verify_release.sh, which warns when published .signet.ca.pem copies differ from the live one).

Signet's recommendation: adopt cloister's envelope scheme (KEK from a Worker secret via HKDF, per-encrypt AES-256-GCM) for the CA master and delegated JWT keys rather than inventing a second mechanism. Reusing the audited path is cheaper than justifying a divergent one, and it removes the "root weaker than leaves" claim outright instead of narrowing it.

Sequencing: signet does NOT treat this as a gate on its v0.3.0 artifact release — the release train's dependency on the authority is the enrollment path being live, not the custody mechanism. But it does constrain claims: signet's release notes will not describe the authority's key custody as hardened while this stands. If notme prefers to defer, signet asks only that the deferral be explicit and dated rather than left open, since signet's own supply-chain posture inherits from this root.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
HARD CONSTRAINT FROM CLOISTER — enabling the KEK envelope requires its RECOVERY PATH exercised first, and the reason is an availability coupling that was not previously written down anywhere.

WHAT CLOISTER SHIPPED. Per their ADR-0053, `resolveCABundle` throws `CaUnavailableError` → JSON-RPC `-32005` when there is no anchor. The only "off" switch is `CLOISTER_MODE=dev` with no authority configured at all; every other configuration enforces, including "no authority", which enforces and then fails closed at bundle resolution. A request with no reachable bundle FAILS LOUDLY with a code naming the cause — not degraded verification, not skipped verification.

THE CONSEQUENCE THEY NAMED AND ACCEPTED: notme's availability is now CLOISTER'S availability. They do not degrade, so a notme outage is a cloister outage. They judged that correct against the alternative — a leaked master key forging every lease retroactively — and it is the right trade. But it means notme's uptime is a hard dependency of a downstream system, which changes how this bead should be sequenced.

WHY THAT BLOCKS THIS BEAD AS CURRENTLY SCOPED: encrypting the CA master key at rest reads like a local hardening improvement. Through this coupling it is not. If the KEK source is unreachable at DO boot — misconfiguration, a rotated secret, a platform issue — the authority cannot serve, cloister does not degrade, and cloister stops. So the failure mode of a key-encryption change is a downstream outage rather than a local error.

WHAT THIS BEAD NOW NEEDS BEFORE THE ENVELOPE IS TURNED ON:
1. A REHEARSED RECOVERY PATH, not a documented one. What an operator does when the KEK is unreachable, executed at least once against staging, with the time-to-recover measured rather than estimated.
2. AN EXPLICIT DECISION on boot behaviour when NOTME_KEK_SECRET is absent but NOTME_KEY_STORAGE=encrypted. `signing-authority.ts:162` currently hard-errors, which is correct in isolation and is exactly the case that propagates. It should stay a hard error — silently falling back to unencrypted would be worse — but it must be a decision on record rather than an artifact.
3. STAGING FIRST, and left running long enough to cross a DO eviction, since the failure surfaces on cold start rather than at deploy.

RELATED: the same coupling argues for finishing `notme-9f2f79`'s convergence work, because "notme is down" and "notme is mid-deploy and traffic is split across builds" look identical from cloister's side today.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: Persistent-mode private keys (keys.private_jwk and delegated_jwt_keys.private_jwk) are envelope-encrypted at rest with a KEK derived from a Worker secret, matching cloister/vault/src/crypto.ts. validateKeyStorageConfig no longer throws for mode "encrypted". A test asserts the stored column does not contain the JWK "d" parameter in cleartext. `task worker:check` green.

title: Adopt leyline-mcp-descriptor for server.json once it supports multi-package producers
description:
Follow-on to notme-83706a. Blocked on `ley-line-open-44cc45`.

notme's `server.json` is hand-written and `scripts/check-image-versions.ts`
hand-implements the ADR-0041 §2 invariant. ley-line-open ships
`leyline-mcp-descriptor`, whose stated purpose is "Shared by every ART producer
so the coverage invariants are not reimplemented per repo" — but it cannot
represent notme today:

- singular `oci_image` / `oci_version`; notme publishes **two** images
- `transport_type` / `transport_url` required, and tool/group coverage
  validated; notme has no MCP surface at all

Neither is it published to crates.io, and adoption across the ecosystem is
currently zero (checked 2026-07-28), so nothing is lost by waiting.

## When ley-line-open-44cc45 lands

1. Replace the hand-written `server.json` with generated output, keeping the
   `_meta.art.cloister/v1` bundle block (notme-identity + notme-proxy tiers and
   rationale) — that content is notme's, not derivable.
2. Fold `scripts/check-image-versions.ts` down to whatever the descriptor does
   not cover. Two checks are notme-specific and likely stay regardless:
   - melange recipe versions track the tag, including the apk `-` → `_`
     spelling (apk reserves `-r<N>`, so `0.1.0-rc1` must be written
     `0.1.0_rc1` — melange rejects the former outright)
   - assertion against the *pushed* `VERSION`, shared with `image:publish`
3. Add a `gen:server-json:check` drift gate to CI, mirroring ley-line-open's.

Worth weighing at that point: adopting means a Rust build dependency in a repo
whose tooling is otherwise TS/JS (`scripts/*.ts` via tsx). If the descriptor
stays unpublished and must be built from a path/git dep, the duplication may
still be the cheaper trade — decide on the evidence then, not now.

## Do not lose

Whatever happens, the two ADR-0041 halves must stay enforced together: reject a
tagged/digest-pinned identifier AND reject an absent version. ley-line-open
v0.11.2 shipped through a guard that did only the first.

comments.text:
RESOLVED as acceptance option (b) — adoption rejected, with the measured
reason recorded rather than assumed.

The blocking dependency did land: `ley-line-open-44cc45` (multi-package) and
`ley-line-open-0135fa` (artifact-only mode) are both done, shipped in v0.13.0
as SHA256SUMS-verified per-platform binaries. So this was genuinely decidable
today, and I decided it on evidence from running the thing.

## What running the emitter showed

Fed it a notme descriptor. Its rendered output has no `title`, no
`websiteUrl`, and `_meta` is a closed two-field struct. Generating notme's
file would drop five things:

  1. `title`
  2. `websiteUrl`
  3. `_meta."io.github.agentic-research.notme/surface"`
  4. `_meta."io.github.agentic-research.notme/packages"`
  5. `_meta."art.cloister/v1".bundles[]`

(5) is the one that decides it, and it is worse than "not supported": the
crate uses that SAME `art.cloister/v1` key for tool-group claims, and omits
the key entirely when there are no groups. notme has no groups — so a
generated file drops ~40 lines of hypervisor-tier bundle topology
(ADR-0011/0018/0005) SILENTLY rather than erroring. This bead's own item 1
anticipated needing to keep that block; the emitter has no slot for it.

Secondary, both as predicted here: the crate is still not on crates.io (the
publish queue is staged pending an explicit go), and its own docs say "This
input shape WILL change" re: the transport scalars.

## What was adopted anyway — the part that mattered

The SHAPE, which is the actual interop surface. notme's `artifacts` array is
byte-identical to the emitter's rendered output, diff-verified:

    diff <(jq -S '._meta["io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided"]' llo-rendered.json) \
         <(jq -S '...' server.json)   -> IDENTICAL

So notme is conformant without being coupled, and a Rust build dependency
stays out of a TS/JS repo — the trade this bead flagged as worth weighing.

## "Do not lose" — kept, and extended

Both ADR-0041 halves still enforced together (absent version fatal, tagged
identifier fatal, per-entry). Item 3's drift gate landed as `task server:check`
on every PR. And the two notme-specific checks this bead predicted would stay
regardless did stay: the apk `-` → `_` recipe spelling, and the assertion
against the pushed `VERSION`.

Re-open if the descriptor grows an arbitrary-`_meta` passthrough — that single
change would flip this decision, since everything else already lines up.

Detail in notme-38044e. Closing.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: Either (a) server.json is generated by leyline-mcp-descriptor with a CI drift gate and check-image-versions.ts reduced to the notme-specific checks, `task version:check VERSION=<tag>` still passing; or (b) a comment on this bead recording the measured reason adoption was rejected, with the duplication accepted deliberately.

title: Drop NPM_TOKEN from publish-dpop.yml in favor of npm OIDC trusted publishing
description:
.github/workflows/publish-dpop.yml ends with `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}` on the `task dpop:ci-publish` step. The job already requests `id-token: write` for provenance, so the OIDC plumbing exists — this is a registry-side trusted-publisher configuration plus removing the env line.

Worth doing here first, and pointedly: notme is the repo whose entire purpose is eliminating stored credentials. Its own gha-identity.yml reusable workflow is documented as OIDC -> octo-sts scoped token + bridge cert, explicitly "eliminates stored PATs", and signet consumes it to eliminate SIGNET_MASTER_KEY. The npm publish path is the one place a long-lived secret survives in this repo.

canonical-hours has the identical issue in publish-vespers.yml (canonical-hours-4effd2); same fix, and whichever lands first should record what the registry-side trusted-publisher setup actually required so the second is mechanical.

Verify the provenance attestation still attaches after the change — trusted publishing and provenance interact, and losing provenance to remove a token would be a bad trade.

Surfaced 2026-07-27 while surveying release stories across all ten repos; recorded in vigil's release-contract design (section 8.1) at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-release-contract-design.md in the vigil repo.

title: worker: revive revocation.test.ts (currently dormant)
description:
worker/src/revocation.test.ts is checked in but neither runs nor typechecks:
- vitest.config.ts only globs `src/__tests__/**/*.test.ts` — file is at the wrong path
- The file imports from `cloudflare:test` (vitest-pool-workers) and uses `env.REVOCATION` DO binding — neither is wired up in the project's TS config or vitest pool

Currently excluded from tsconfig.json so `tsc --noEmit` passes. Documented in the file's header.

To revive:
1. Move the file to `worker/src/__tests__/revocation.test.ts`
2. Update `vitest.config.ts` to set `pool: '@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers'` and `poolOptions.workers.wrangler.configPath: './wrangler.toml'`
3. Add a module augmentation declaring `ProvidedEnv` with the REVOCATION DurableObjectNamespace (and any other bindings the test touches)
4. Drop `src/revocation.test.ts` from tsconfig `exclude`
5. Confirm the test runs under vitest and the assertions match current revocation.ts behavior

This adds DO-level coverage for the revocation flow which is currently only covered by adversarial integration tests at the worker level.

comments.text:
Investigated during the security/completeness loop. Deferring with sharper scope:

**Blockers found in the path:**
1. `wrangler.toml` has `[[vpc_services]] binding = "VPC_AUTH"` — miniflare (which vitest-pool-workers uses) does not natively support vpc_services bindings. Pointing the pool at wrangler.toml directly will likely fail at miniflare init.
2. `vitest 4.1.2` + `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers ^0.13.5` — the codemod package included is `vitest-v3-to-v4`, suggesting v0.13+ targets vitest 4 but the migration is recent. README is one paragraph, no inline config example.

**Recommended path (next agent):**
- Don't touch the existing `vitest.config.ts` — it owns the 137-test suite that runs in default node pool. Keep that path stable.
- Add a separate `vitest.workers.config.ts` with `pool: '@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers'` and an inline `miniflare: { ... }` object that declares ONLY the bindings the test needs (REVOCATION DO + CA_BUNDLE_CACHE KV — no ASSETS, no VPC, no SIGNING_AUTHORITY).
- Add a `test:workers` npm script: `vitest run --config vitest.workers.config.ts`.
- Move `src/revocation.test.ts` → `src/__tests__/revocation.test.ts`.
- Add a top-level `declare module "cloudflare:test" { interface ProvidedEnv { REVOCATION: DurableObjectNamespace; CA_BUNDLE_CACHE: KVNamespace; } }` in the test file or a shared types file.
- Drop the `src/revocation.test.ts` exclude from `tsconfig.json`.
- Ensure CI runs both `npm test` and `npm run test:workers` separately.

**Why not now:** the failure mode is that `vitest run` would error out before any test runs if miniflare can't initialize. That breaks the loop's invariant of "137/137 vitest still green" on every commit. A dedicated session can verify miniflare's binding tolerance and adjust without that constraint.
