title: red-team:trust-root — validateCommitment signs float64 timestamp_ms: every receipt is non-canonical, every conformant commitment is rejected
description:
Filed from adversarial review of PR #61 (branch `notme-c1b7fd-receipt-signing`), trust-root lens.

## Location
- `worker/src/receipts/commitment.ts:20-26` (Encoder), `:36-42` (Decoder), `:118-126` (`requireUint`), `:229` (the equality check)

## Summary
The "canonically re-encode and require byte equality" gate — the single defense that makes signing with the CA master key safe — is pinned to **cbor-x's encoder behavior**, not to RFC 8949 §4.2. cbor-x diverges from §4.2 for integers >= 2^32, and `timestamp_ms` is unix **milliseconds**, so every real commitment crosses that boundary.

Empirically (cbor-x 1.6.4, the pinned version):
- `cbor.encode(1775000000000)` -> `fb4279d463e9600000` — CBOR **major type 7 float64**, not the shortest-form uint64 `1b0000019d463e9600`.
- `cborDecoder.decode(0x1b ...)` -> **BigInt**, which `requireUint` rejects (`typeof v !== "number"` -> `FIELD_NOT_UINT`).

## Proof (against the real module, esbuild-bundled and run under node)
Hand-built RFC 8949 §4.2 canonical commitment (what fxamacker/cbor `CanonicalEncOptions`, ciborium, or any conformant encoder emits):
```
...6c74696d657374616d705f6d73 1b0000019d463e9600
=> REJECTED: FIELD_NOT_UINT - "timestamp_ms" must be a non-negative CBOR integer
```
The form notme actually accepts and signs:
```
...6c74696d657374616d705f6d73 fb4279d463e9600000
=> ACCEPTED and SIGNED
```
Same 243-byte length, diverging at offset 234. All other seven fields encode canonically; only `timestamp_ms` is wrong.

## Why this is a trust-root defect, not just interop
`interlace-spec/0.2.0-draft/RECEIPTS.md` §2.1 types `timestamp_ms` as `<uint>` and requires `canonical_cbor()` = RFC 8949 §4.2 with "shortest length form for integers". §3.1 "canonicalization landmines" is explicit: **"Floats and NaN are forbidden... canonical receipt schemas in this spec contain no float fields at all... always use uint milliseconds rather than float seconds."** notme emits precisely the forbidden construct, and §3.1 also says conformant decoders MUST reject non-conformant encodings.

Consequences:
1. **The non-repudiation property the PR exists to establish does not hold.** §2.2.2 V-archival audit decodes `commitment_cbor` strictly; a float where a uint is specified fails. Receipts notme signs are not usable as evidence by an independent auditor — the entire point of moving the key into notme.
2. **The ADR's central claim is false.** `docs/design/014-receipt-signing.md`: "a receipt notme signed is canonically encoded, so a verifier recomputing the digest gets the same answer." It is guaranteed non-canonical.
3. **Fails closed for conformant callers.** A Go/Rust cloister emitting spec-canonical commitments gets `FIELD_NOT_UINT` on 100% of requests. The path only works because cloister also pins `cbor-x ^1.6.4` — cbor-x validated against itself.
4. **The signable byte set is defined by a caret-ranged third-party encoder.** What the CA master key will sign is `{b : cborX.encode(cborX.decode(b)) == b}`, not "canonical CBOR". A cbor-x minor bump that fixes this very bug silently changes the accepted set and makes every previously issued receipt unreproducible.

## Why the tests missed it
`worker/src/__tests__/receipt-commitment.test.ts` (17 passing) and `worker/src/receipt-signer.do.test.ts` both build fixtures with the same cbor-x Encoder they validate against, so the fixed point is trivially satisfied. RECEIPTS.md §7 requires `receipt-canonical-bytes.json` with "`timestamp_ms` near uint8/uint16/uint32 boundaries" — that pinned vector does not exist here and would have caught this immediately.

## Why `bundleCanonical` escaped
`worker/src/revocation.ts:250` feeds the same cbor-x Encoder and claims byte-parity with signet's `BundleCanonical`. It survives only because `issuedAt` is in **seconds** (~1.75e9 < 2^32, encoded `0x1a`), not milliseconds. So the comment in `commitment.ts:18-19` ("Encoder settings must match `bundleCanonical`") is false comfort: identical settings, different value ranges, different conformance outcome. That path breaks in 2106.

## Fix
Do not delegate the signing input to cbor-x's encoder. The schema is eight fixed fields — hand-roll the ~40-line RFC 8949 §4.2 encoder (definite-length map, shortest-form uint header, byte strings, text keys pre-sorted) so "what the CA master key will sign" is defined by the spec rather than by a dependency's incidental behavior. Correspondingly accept `number | bigint` in `requireUint` (cbor-x surfaces `0x1b` as BigInt) and normalize before the range checks. Then pin the RECEIPTS.md §7 `receipt-canonical-bytes.json` vector — including a `timestamp_ms` above 2^32 — as a cross-implementation contract test, the way `key-id.ts` pins its ADR-012 conformance vector.

## Confidence
High (9/10). Reproduced against the shipped module; spec text is explicit and normative.

## Reproduction
Bundle the module and run the two-arm PoC:
```
cd worker && ./node_modules/.bin/esbuild src/receipts/commitment.ts --bundle --format=esm --platform=node --outfile=/tmp/commitment.mjs
# then call validateCommitment with a hand-built 0x1b-form commitment (rejected)
# and with cbor.encode(map) (accepted, 0xfb float64 tail)
```

comments.text:
CLOSING — both halves fixed and verified against merged main, including the re-encode half cloister could not confirm from outside.

DECODE HALF (the one cloister could see): `requireUint` accepts bigint. cbor-x decodes a shortest-form uint64 to BigInt, and the old `typeof v !== "number"` guard therefore rejected 100% of commitments from any spec-conformant encoder.

RE-ENCODE HALF (the one they asked about): cbor-x is no longer used for encoding at all. `commitment.ts:21` imports `encodeCanonicalMap` from a hand-rolled RFC 8949 §4.2 encoder (worker/src/receipts/canonical-cbor.ts), and `:319` uses it for the re-encode. `grep -n Encoder worker/src/receipts/commitment.ts` returns nothing — the module imports `Decoder` only. cbor-x cannot emit a float64 into the signing input because it no longer emits the signing input.

Proved rather than reasoned, running the merged encoder:

    ts 4294967295     head 70   (uint32)  contains /fb[0-9a-f]{16}/: false
    ts 4294967296     head 1b   (uint64)  contains /fb[0-9a-f]{16}/: false
    ts 1775000000000  head 1b   (uint64)  contains /fb[0-9a-f]{16}/: false
    ts <now>          head 1b   (uint64)  contains /fb[0-9a-f]{16}/: false

Exactly at and across the 2^32 boundary, which is where the bug lived.

WHY THE HAND-ROLL RATHER THAN A CBOR-X FLAG: what the CA master key signs should be defined by the spec, not by a dependency's incidental behaviour. Under the old arrangement a cbor-x minor bump fixing this very bug would silently change the signable byte set and make every prior receipt unreproducible.

THE JOINT VECTOR IS THE RIGHT THING TO KEEP ASKING ABOUT, and cloister is right that it is what catches this on both sides. notme pins the same 12 cases at worker/src/__tests__/vectors/receipt-canonical-bytes.json, generated by encoding each input with BOTH cloister's canonicalCbor(commitmentCborMap(...)) and notme's encodeCanonicalMap(...) and requiring byte-for-byte agreement — 0 disagreements across all 12. Cloister asserts no float64 heads via not.toMatch(/fb[0-9a-f]{16}/); notme asserts the same property as not.toContain(0xfb) plus a full byte-equality check per vector.

The reason this bug shipped with 17 green tests is worth keeping attached to the closure: every fixture was built with the same encoder being validated, which is a fixed point rather than a conformance check — any self-consistent encoder passes it, including a wrong one. It was found by running cloister's real output through notme's validator. The joint vector exists so that is a standing check rather than a one-off.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: `worker/src/__tests__/receipt-commitment.test.ts` contains a test asserting that a hand-built RFC 8949 §4.2 canonical commitment with `timestamp_ms` encoded as `0x1b` uint64 (value > 2^32) is ACCEPTED, and that the bytes returned by `validateCommitment` contain no major-type-7 (0xf9/0xfa/0xfb) item. Run: `cd worker && pnpm vitest run src/__tests__/receipt-commitment.test.ts`

title: P0: TS adopts canonical CBOR for CABundle signing canonicalization (per ADR-010 + signet protocol)
description:
Implements `docs/design/010-cross-language-canonical-encoding.md`.

## Scope

ONLY the cryptographic canonical bytes (Ed25519 sign/verify input). JSON stays load-bearing for everything else (HTTP API, KV storage, DO blob columns, DPoP/JWT) — that matches signet's own architecture.

## What changes

1. Add `cbor-x` to `worker/package.json` (Workers V8 compatible, RFC 8949 §4.2 deterministic encoding).
2. Replace `worker/src/revocation.ts::bundleCanonical()` body with CBOR-canonical encoding using integer-keyed map matching signet exactly:
   ```
   1 → Epoch     (uint64)
   2 → Seqno     (uint64)
   3 → Keys      (map[string][]byte)
   4 → KeyID     (string)
   5 → PrevKeyID (string, "" if absent)
   6 → IssuedAt  (int64)
   ```
3. Replace inline duplicate at `worker/src/signing-authority.ts:443-447` with import of the shared `bundleCanonical()` function (closes companion bead notme-XXX P3 dedupe).
4. Cross-runtime fixture suite at `schema/fixtures/cabundle-*.bin` + `*.expected.hex` — signet Go produces fixture; notme TS asserts byte-equality.
5. Migration: dual-encode for one rotation cycle (writer signs both JSON-canonical and CBOR-canonical, verifier accepts either), then drop JSON.

## Acceptance

- `bundleCanonical()` output for a known-fixture bundle byte-equals signet's `encMode.Marshal(message)` output.
- All existing tests pass (`npx vitest run`).
- New cross-runtime fixture test asserts byte equality.
- Schema docstring matches reality.

## Verification ladder

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. `npx vitest run` 332/332 + new fixture test.
3. Manual: take a notme-issued bundle, run signet Go's verifier against it. Should succeed.
4. Manual: take a signet Go-issued bundle, run notme TS verifier against it. Should succeed.

## Anchors

- `docs/design/010-cross-language-canonical-encoding.md` — the decision.
- `signet/pkg/revocation/checker.go:168-188` — byte-for-byte target.
- `signet/pkg/revocation/cabundle/https_fetcher.go` — confirms JSON is transport, CBOR is signing-only.
- `worker/src/revocation.ts:159-166` — function to replace.
- `worker/src/signing-authority.ts:443-447` — inline duplicate to remove.
- `schema/identity.capnp` — already updated (docstring fix landed with ADR-010).
- Replaces `notme-803923` (closed in favor of this + the two siblings below).

comments.text:
**Done in commit 61fd857** (branch `notme-803923-cbor-canonical`).

- `bundleCanonical()` now emits canonical CBOR (RFC 8949 §4.2) with integer-keyed map matching signet/pkg/revocation/checker.go:168-188 byte-for-byte.
- cbor-x ^1.6.4 added with explicit options (`mapsAsObjects: false`, `useRecords: false`, `tagUint8Array: false`) to ensure RFC 8949 strict canonical output.
- Inner Keys map sorted per RFC 8949 §4.2 (length-then-bytewise lex on UTF-8 keys).
- Base64 → Uint8Array conversion so CBOR encodes values as bytes (major type 2), matching Go's `[]byte`.
- Tests at `src/__tests__/bundle-canonical.test.ts` (5 cases, all pass):
  - 6-entry CBOR map header
  - Determinism
  - TS field-order independence
  - prevKeyId='' encoded as empty string (matches Go zero value)
  - **Hand-computed fixture: 25 bytes byte-for-byte locked**. Future cross-runtime gate: signet Go-side test produces same bytes; this test becomes the verification check.
- Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npx vitest run` 337/337 pass (was 332; +5 new tests).

Migration note (deferred): the dual-encode rotation strategy from ADR-010 is NOT implemented in this commit. The cutover is hard. Acceptable because:
1. notme is currently in dev (no production user signatures to orphan).
2. CABundle is regenerated every 4min via SigningAuthority alarm, so any bundle with old JSON-canonical signature gets replaced within one alarm cycle.

If a production deployment with persistent JSON-canonical signed bundles needs migration, file a follow-on bead for the dual-encode-and-drop choreography.

title: P1: schema sync drift — capnp-to-ts.ts silently degrades on unknown features
description:
Independent of wire-format work (`docs/design/010-...`). This is type-sync correctness, not signature canonicalization.

## The hole

`schema/codegen/capnp-to-ts.ts` is a 280-LOC hand-rolled regex parser. It silently drops:

- `Float*` types (no Float32, Float64)
- Smaller-than-32 ints (no Int8, UInt8, Int16, UInt16)
- `AnyPointer`
- Annotations (e.g. workerd-style `$compatEnableDate`)
- Groups
- Generics
- Interfaces

When unknown features appear in `schema/identity.capnp`, the generator falls through to `unknown` / `z.unknown()` rather than erroring. A future schema edit that uses any of these can ship without anyone noticing — runtime Zod validation passes whatever, downstream code thinks it has type safety it doesn't.

## Two fix options

**(A) Replace with proper capnp toolchain.**
- `capnp-ts` library (npm). Real capnp wire format support.
- May or may not work on Workers V8; needs vetting.
- Heaviest. Fully fixes the silent-degradation problem AND opens the door to using real capnp wire format if ever desired (we explicitly chose CBOR per ADR-010, so this isn't load-bearing — but parity with the Go-side `capnpc-go` output becomes possible).

**(B) Fail-loud-on-unknown-features.**
- Keep `capnp-to-ts.ts` simple but add an exhaustive switch on capnp types.
- Unknown features throw at codegen time with a helpful error message ("AnyPointer not supported by capnp-to-ts.ts; consider option A or rewrite the schema").
- Cheaper. Doesn't fix the underlying limitation; just makes drift impossible.

Most likely the right answer is (B) for now (cheap, immediately stops drift), with a follow-up bead for (A) if the schema ever needs features (B) doesn't support.

## Acceptance

- (A): `gen/ts/identity.ts` is byte-equal output of a real capnp toolchain run; CI runs the codegen + asserts no drift; capnp toolchain version pinned.
- (B): adding a `Float64` field to `schema/identity.capnp` and running `task schema:ts` errors out with a clear message; exhaustive type list in the generator's switch is documented as the supported subset.

## Anchors

- `schema/codegen/capnp-to-ts.ts` — the parser.
- `schema/identity.capnp` — the source.
- `gen/ts/identity.ts` — the output.
- `ley-line-open/docs/decades/T8/capnp-rtfm-findings.md` — capnp tooling research.

Replaces part of `notme-803923` (the schema-sync portion).

title: Reshape mintBridgeCertPair into /identity/lease — {scope, peer} mint endpoint
description:
Per cloister ADR-0006 draft (cloister-bc8b0f). REVISED — the master CA + cert minting are already shipped; this is a reshape, not a new build.

The notme worker already has:
- `SigningAuthority` DO — Ed25519 master CA, key born-in-CF, never leaves
- `cert-authority.ts::mintBridgeCertPair` — mints 5-min ephemeral P-256 cert pair (mTLS + signing) signed by Ed25519 master, with X.509 KeyUsage + EKU + custom-OID extensions
- `cert-exchange.ts::handleCertExchange` — endpoint shape that takes a proof and returns a cert pair
- `revocation.ts` — epoch-bundle CA rotation

The Interlace lease shape is a narrower variant of `mintBridgeCertPair`: single signing cert, scoped, peer-bound.

## Endpoint
`POST /identity/lease`
Request:
```json
{ "scope": "bead_create:/repos/rosary", "peer": "sha256:...", "ttl_seconds": 300 }
```
Response: ephemeral signing cert (DER) + ephemeral private key. Same wire shape as the signing half of `mintBridgeCertPair`.

## Auth on the mint
Caller authenticates with an existing notme proof (DPoP / OIDC token via `auth/verify-proof.ts` — already shipped). The mint endpoint does NOT require a Signet cert (chicken-and-egg).

## Cert extensions to add
- Existing custom-OID arc (`1.3.6.1.4.1.99999`) already used by `mintBridgeCertPair` — extend with:
  - `interlace-peer` (peer fingerprint from request)
  - `interlace-scope` (scope from request, opaque string)
- Reuse the same DER encoding helpers in `cert-authority.ts`.

## Scope grammar
Opaque to notme — caller-supplied string, signed verbatim. Cloister parses + checks. Optional notme-side allowlist policy if desired (env-configurable list of permitted scope prefixes per principal).

## Success criteria
- ~50–100 LOC delta in worker — new route + scope-grammar wrapper around existing mint.
- Round-trip test: `POST /identity/lease` → verify with leyline-sign WASM (per ley-line-* sibling) → cert chains to master, scope present, TTL bounded.
- No changes to `SigningAuthority` DO. No new master keys. No new revocation primitives.

## Out of scope
- Revocation broadcast (open Q from ADR-0006 — separate bead).
- Multi-master / federation.

comments.text:
CROSS-CUTTING PATTERN worth recording at the epic level, because it has now produced three findings this session and cloister independently named it as a fourth.

THE PATTERN: an artifact asserting a property of its own provenance that nothing verified.
1. notme-ebc9af — a bridge cert stamped authMethod:"passkey" for any session kind, so an invite-authed cert claimed a human touched an authenticator. Provenance asserted, not established. FIXED by deriving it from the session.
2. notme-c0a4aa — .github/workflows/gha-identity.yml advertised outputs (notme_token, expires_in) the action never emitted, and action.yml advertised github_token that src never sets. An always-empty output is an interface asserting a capability it does not have. FIXED, with a gate covering all four directions.
3. notme-28959a — action/dist/index.js embedded undici 6.25.0 while the lockfile and the workspace override both said 6.28.0. The committed artifact asserted a build it was not the product of. Bundle REBUILT; the durable half (CI rebuild-and-diff, plus advancing both consumers' pins) is still open.
4. Cloister's addition (notme-600df1): wimse://notme.bot/passkey/<principalId> names a workload identity after a human ceremony. Even when the ceremony genuinely happened, the identifier claims to name a machine while what was verified was a person — and the identity is presented later, unattended, when no human is present.

Cloister names a fifth in their own repo: receipts committing to bytes rather than origins.

WHY THIS BELONGS ON THE EPIC. Goal Zero's exit criteria are about having no UNKNOWN release blockers. Each of these was invisible for the same reason — the artifact said the right thing, and nothing compared the claim to the thing claimed. The general gate is: for every self-describing artifact (cert extension, workflow output, committed bundle, identity URI), is there something that would fail if the description stopped being true? That question found all four; none of them were found by tests, reviews of intent, or reading the code for correctness.

Related and independently observed by the identity audit: the sibling pattern where a GREEN TEST proves a real property of a path production does not take (bootstrap-code.do.test.ts establishing its admin via the one function the passkey flow never calls; the rotation-grace test guarding a branch no token can enter, still open as N10). Same root — a check that does not touch the thing it appears to check.

comments.text:
## Documentation-honesty audit (criterion A) — 2026-08-06

GOAL-ZERO-STATUS §6 recorded that `worker/THREAT_MODEL.md` and the ADRs had never been checked against what ships, and predicted the audit would find more artifacts asserting properties nothing verified. It did — nine, filed below. Every one is verified against production code, not against another document.

Method note, because it changed a conclusion twice: `grep` under-reports here, so every zero-result claim is confirmed with `git grep` and a `find … -exec grep -l` sweep. The two deliberate test conventions (`it.fails` marking a gap, fixtures built without the code under test) were treated as correct and are not reported.

### The load-bearing one

**`notme-8d3018` (P1) — the revocation verifier ships unwired.** `checkRevocation`, `verifyBundleSignature`, `isBundleStale` and the `RevocationAuthority` DO have **no production caller**. `worker.ts` never imports `src/revocation.ts` (it re-exports the DO class only so wrangler can bind it) and never references `env.REVOCATION`. The sole production consumer of the cached bundle, `ensureCurrentCABundle` (`src/internal-ca-bundle.ts:17-35`), `JSON.parse`s the KV value with no signature, seqno or staleness check.

ARCHITECTURE.md's security-model diagram nonetheless draws `REV` inside the edge-plane request chain `CERT → WAF → VER → REV`, and README/ARCHITECTURE both headline identities as "scoped, ephemeral, **revocable**". THREAT_MODEL §3 books four defences against it. `revocation.do.test.ts` gives the module 14 real-DO tests — the §7 pattern at full strength: correct code, excellent tests, zero request paths.

This is criterion (C) stated as if it were already met. The docs half is unblocked today; the code half is `notme-77a024`'s to decide.

### Tests that verify nothing

**`notme-8da0a3` (P1) — `routes.test.ts` and `cert-gha.test.ts` import no production code at all.** Verified by scanning every test file for static *and* dynamic production imports; nine scored zero, seven of which legitimately read real artifacts (config, HTML, git state, real DOs). These two read nothing. `routes.test.ts` contains `expect(true).toBe(true)` twice, `expect("identity authority").not.toBe("agent identity")`, and `expect(blockedPaths).toContain(path)` over the array it just declared; its header says the tests "should FAIL until routes are wired into worker.ts" — the routes have been wired for months and the tests never failed because they assert nothing about them. `cert-gha.test.ts` reimplements the owner allowlist, the rate-limit arithmetic, the JTI TTL formula and `getConfig` inside the test file, while `getAllowedOwners` sits exported at `worker.ts:591` unused. Five THREAT_MODEL rows point here. The defences themselves are all real — this is unverified, not unprotected.

**`notme-8fb37f` (P2) — three runaway-alarm rows still say "(pending notme-c38bb6)".** That bead closed 2026-07-22, as did its follow-up `notme-97b3ff`; the vitest-pool-workers harness it gated now runs 15 `.do.test.ts` files. No test touches the alarm code — `rg -i alarm` over the whole suite returns one comment. The circuit breaker, the idempotent reschedule and the driftRatio counter are all implemented and all unexercised, defending a failure mode whose stated cost is an unbounded CF invoice. Same stale excuse appears at `threat-model.test.ts:398`, where `applySeqnoRule` is reimplemented inside the test file (real coverage does now exist in `revocation.do.test.ts:127-195`).

### Claims stronger than the deployment

**`notme-8e0f3a` (P1) — `/api/docs` is live and documents a superseded API.** Both cert response examples include a `private_key` field. `rg -n "private_key"` over the whole repo returns three hits, all HTML — no production route emits it, and `/cert/gha` requires caller-supplied `public_keys` + PoP proofs (`worker.ts:676-741`), so the documented curl returns 400. It also documents `POST /exchange-token` and `POST /api/cert/register`, neither of which is served, and a discovery sample advertising `oidc_token_exchange`/`github_pat` when `AUTHORITY_GRANT_TYPES` is `["github_actions_oidc","dpop"]`. `/token`, `/authorize` and DPoP are absent entirely. Notable inversion: the page understates security on the one property the secretless design exists to provide. `src/as-metadata.ts` is the standard the page should be held to — it documents *why* each field is deliberately omitted and separates policy constraints from truth constraints.

**`notme-900e28` (P2) — §2 claims "10 certs/repo/hour"; `CERT_LIMITER` is 10 per 60 **seconds**.** 600/hour, 60× the documented cap. CF's `period` accepts only 10 or 60, so the hourly figure is not expressible as a binding — it is the replaced KV limiter's number. Its constants still sit in `getConfig` (`worker.ts:576-578`), computed and never read.

**`notme-a8ac8f` (P2) — ADR-007 promises a `kek-entropy-check` that does not exist.** The adversarial-test table says `NOTME_KEK_SECRET=weak` fails startup, "secret too short", under invariant #3. Neither `validateKeyStorageConfig` (`platform.ts:73-85`) nor `deriveKek` (`key-encryption.ts:75-81`) rejects anything but empty. `NOTME_KEY_STORAGE=encrypted NOTME_KEK_SECRET=weak` boots and seals the CA key under four characters — HKDF stretches, it does not add entropy, which is `deriveKek`'s own argument for rejecting the empty case. Also folded in: five of six `invariant #N` comments in `adversarial.test.ts` cite the wrong invariant against ADR-007's numbered list, so the doc→evidence trail ARCHITECTURE.md advertises lands on the wrong test.

**`notme-a040c1` (P2) — ADR-010's hard-cutover decision leans on a fail-closed path nothing calls.** *"revocation checks fail closed during that window (per `revocation.ts::isBundleStale`)"* — same dead module as `8d3018`. The conclusion may stand on its other ground; the safety argument does not. **Correction already committed** (`57d5a24`) as a dated CORRECTION block in ADR-010, matching ADR-008 §299's format. Worth noting the irony: ADR-010's own subject is a docstring that claimed a guarantee ("Cap'n Proto's deterministic binary format guarantees this") nothing delivered.

### Bookkeeping, still criterion (A)

**`notme-8eed12` (P2) — 28 of ~53 THREAT_MODEL test identifiers exist nowhere in the repo**, while the file asserts "each test name maps to a row in the tables above". They split into label drift (the defence *is* tested under another name — `authorize.redirect-token.unbound` really lives at `dpop-nonce.do.test.ts:271-293`, and so on) and genuine absence (all three CORS rows, both rate-limit rows, `authorize.session.fixation`, `routing.cache.vary`). The doc gives a reader no way to tell which is which. Includes a related inaccuracy: §6 says "6 domains, no wildcards"; `worker.ts:1570` also admits any `http://localhost:` origin.

**`notme-8e6863` (P2) — §9 documents 18 vault defences for a package ADR-012 deleted.** `git ls-files vault/` is empty. 18 of ~110 rows describe code this repo does not contain, and cloister has since diverged (3-tier KEK scoping notme never had), so the frozen text is not a proxy for cloister's either.

**`notme-9087aa` (P3) — README endpoint table says `/cert` and `/cert/gha` return access tokens**; both mint X.509 cert pairs. Plus `vault/` listed twice with a dead link, `gen/ts` described as the shared SDK (that is `packages/dpop`), "ADRs 005-009" when there are fifteen, and test counts about a third of actual.

### Checked and found honest — recorded so coverage is auditable

ADR-014's byte-for-byte equality requirement is genuinely enforced (`receipts/commitment.ts:411`, with a constant-time `bytesEqual`). ADR-015's separate-key-per-delegated-issuer is real (`delegated_jwt_keys` table, `getDelegatedJwtKey`), and its at-rest gap is already fixed and honestly commented. ADR-016's rules 1, 2 and 5 are mechanically enforced by `signing-surfaces.do.test.ts`, and the ADR scopes its own test coverage accurately. ADR-013 is explicit that the legacy `?token=` branch survives until rig ships ("a migration, not a hedge") and the code comment at `worker.ts:2666` agrees. ADR-017's standards block labels the one unverifiable citation **UNVERIFIED** — that is the bar the rest should meet. ADRs 007 and 009 already carry dated audit notes distinguishing intent from running system. `src/as-metadata.ts` documents its deliberate omissions better than any other file in the repo.

### On the NIST pointer raised mid-audit

The AI RMF (nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework) is **not** the artifact backing ADR-019's non-repudiation framing, and shouldn't be swapped in: it is a Govern/Map/Measure/Manage risk framework that does not address agent identity, delegation, authorization or non-repudiation at all. The NCCoE concept paper ADR-019 actually cites remains the right source. The RMF page does corroborate one thing ADR-019 says — it is explicitly voluntary, matching "these are voluntary frameworks — they bind through procurement flow-down, not by their own force." No correction needed.

### What this means for criterion (A)

The documentation-honesty clause is not close to satisfied, but the gap is almost entirely **documentation**, and most of it is unblocked right now. Only two findings have a genuine code half: wiring the bundle verifier (`8d3018`, and even there the doc fix is separable), and the KEK length gate (`a8ac8f`, a few lines). Everything else is text that outran the code and was never re-read. Three sub-findings — `routes.test.ts`, `cert-gha.test.ts`, and the alarm rows — are `it.fails`-shaped in reverse: green tests standing where a gap marker belongs.

Worth adding to §7's defect-pattern list: **"a blocker cited long after it cleared."** Both `notme-c38bb6` (closed two weeks ago) and ADR-010's `isBundleStale` are excuses that outlived their cause, and each made an untested defence look deliberately deferred rather than forgotten.

acceptance_criteria:
Goal Zero is complete when ALL of the following hold.

(A) ORIGINAL CRITERIA — every P0/P1 is closed, linked to a concrete prerequisite, or deliberately deferred; production and preview runtime contracts are exercised; published packages/images have provenance and clean-consumer verification; schema/code/generated artifacts are checked for drift; and a final smoke report proves the Signet/Cloister/LLO integration boundary.

(B) IDENTITY — the authority states what it names. An ADR records whether notme is a human authority bootstrapping workload identity or a workload authority (notme-600df1, answering cloister ADR-0066 Q1/Q2), and the advertised identity no longer varies with the authentication ceremony for a fixed principal (notme-77438b). Registration policy follows from that answer rather than from an inline comment (notme-2c4209).

(C) REVOCATION — a revocation unit exists between "wait for the TTL" and "revoke every credential ever issued" (notme-77a024). The epoch lever is usable independently of key rotation, or the rotation grace window is removed as dead, with the choice recorded. Capability revocation governs passkey users or is documented as not applying to them.

(D) ATTESTATION / THIRD-PARTY VERIFIABILITY — a third party can verify without trusting notme at the moment of the check. Trust does not bottom out in TLS to the issuing host: the root is anchored out of band (notme-8e8836). Issuance is transparent — append-only and tamper-evident, inclusion proof at issuance, third-party inclusion and consistency proofs, verifiable across rotations (notme-907299); RFC 6962 SCTs are the target, evidenced by signet dropping `--no-default-ctfe`. Historical verification works offline from an archive (cloister-ad4eac → cloister-ad7b5a).

(E) BOOTSTRAP — first boot does not require reading a secret out of the logs and cannot be triggered by an unauthenticated stranger (notme-addef9).

DOCUMENTATION HONESTY, applying to all of the above: where a property is deliberately NOT provided, the docs say so plainly rather than implying the stronger property. Several claims in this repo already assert more than the deployment delivers; a release that closes the code gaps and leaves the doc gaps has not met Goal Zero.

title: Goal Zero audit: runtime and deployment proof
description: Review Notme’s Worker/DO operational path. Existing scope to triage: notme-3e22e0, notme-3dac49, notme-6ae724 (runtime contract tests), notme-3e6ecc (Cloudflare API behavior), notme-5c2511 (DO alarm hardening), notme-396aff (browser LLO wasm), notme-2bba44 (token URL exposure), and notme-8bea0d (release runtime). Separate production-required behavior from preview/operator-triggered work.

comments.text:
RUNTIME + DEPLOYMENT PROOF — evidence recorded (PRs #70/#71, branch fix/notme-92a1b9-bootstrap).

AC clause 1, "production and preview behavior tested through the real Worker/DO boundaries": the real-DO pool suite (vitest.workers.config.mts) is now 91 tests across 10 files, including the two added this session — bootstrap-code.do.test.ts (real SigningAuthority lifecycle: single-use, regeneration-while-no-principal, closure after first principal, and the /cert route driven through worker.fetch against the real DO) and the invite/OIDC cases in passkey-cert.do.test.ts. Plain suite is 482.

AC clause 2, "deploy/rollback and runtime contract evidence is recorded": EXERCISED, not asserted. Staging Worker notme-bot-staging deployed and verified 12/12 (versions 4b8bb82c → f6a4ac4b → f4f2468c). Then the full gradual-deployment cycle: `wrangler versions upload --env staging` produced d0cc333f carrying no traffic → `task worker:canary NEW=d0cc333f OLD=f4f2468c PCT=20 ENV=staging` → split confirmed in `wrangler deployments list` (20%/80%) with all 12 verify checks green DURING the split → `task worker:promote NEW=f4f2468c ENV=staging` → 100% on the old id, 12/12 green. Rollback is the promote command pointed at the old id — demonstrated. Preconditions confirmed to fail safe when a version id is omitted. Production verify green 12/12 throughout (read-only; production traffic was never split — the mechanism was rehearsed on staging deliberately).

Gap found and closed while auditing: the canary/promote/versions tasks hardcoded production, so the staging rehearsal would have exercised a DIFFERENT command than the one promoting production. They now take ENV= (commit 59042b0). Second gap closed: nothing enforced the [env.staging] isolation invariants ADR-018 calls load-bearing — staging-isolation.test.ts now gates no-VPC-binding, distinct Worker name, and staging-only hosts, each proven to have teeth by injecting the violation and watching it fail (commit fe6c7da).

Known constraint recorded in ADR-018: a version carrying a new [[migrations]] entry cannot be split-deployed (DO migrations promote atomically, deleted-class migrations do not roll back) — such releases skip canary with the rollback plan reviewed before deploy.

AC clause 3, "every operational P0/P1 closed, linked, or deferred": in progress — the operational P0/P1 sweep is the remaining piece of this bead, pending the parallel audits (c0a445 identity/crypto, c0a4f6 release/package, c0a4aa cross-repo) and the in-flight adversarial reviews of #70/#71. title: Goal Zero audit: identity and cryptographic invariants
description: Review Notme’s security-critical identity surface. Existing scope to triage: notme-89eeed (mTLS binding), notme-976385 and notme-92a1b9 (bootstrap flows), notme-ebc9af (passkey auth claim), notme-41d0d3 (plaintext root keys), notme-2c6d1e (key import), notme-acd503 (receipt replay), notme-b96b4c (schema sync), notme-d86ed3 (DPoP review), and notme-3e9c73 (schema bridge). Keep this tranche focused on invariants required for a supported release.

comments.text:
IDENTITY / CRYPTOGRAPHIC INVARIANT DISPOSITION. The matrix was produced across all six required domains; this records its state NOW, since a third of it moved during the cycle, and dispositions every P0/P1 in those domains.

── DOMAIN STATE, and what changed after the matrix was built ──

BOOTSTRAP — was the audit's single worst domain, now clean, and the fix went further than the audit proposed. It suggested gating on "no principal holds authorityManage"; the shipped predicate counts AUTHENTICATORS (passkey credentials ∪ federated identities), which answers the question the gate actually asks. Then scrutiny of that fix found it was half done: gating the MINT left CONSUMPTION ungated, so a code minted pre-admin and read from the logs stayed redeemable afterwards — and POST /cert mints authorityManage+certMint against one. The invariant is now enforced at both ends. Real-DO coverage replaced four tests that simulated the DO locally, one of which asserted an 8-char code the DO has never generated.

PASSKEY / SESSION BINDING — cert authMethod is derived and validated on BOTH mint paths (the second was found by the dataflow review after the first shipped). resetPasskeyData now rotates the session secret, so a reset revokes what it wipes. RESIDUAL, unfixed and recorded in code at the method: reset is unreachable on any authority with an authenticator, and "corrupted credentials" — the case it claims to serve — still counts as an authenticator. Needs an AUTHENTICATED recovery path, not a code.

KEY CUSTODY — the module is well-tested and INERT IN PRODUCTION. `wrangler secret list` is empty, no deploy workflow sets NOTME_KEK_SECRET, so detectKeyStorage resolves to cf-managed and the CA master plus every delegated JWT key sit as plaintext JWK in DO SQLite. LINKED to notme-41d0d3, which is a DECISION (enable the envelope, or state the posture in SECURITY.md) and explicitly must not be closed by this release. Two sub-findings ride with it: the DO-level seal/read/migrate paths have no test at any level because vitest.workers.config.mts binds no env, and delegated keys can NEVER migrate to sealed storage while a comment says they do.

REPLAY / EPOCH — jti replay is closed atomically inside the singleton DO (INSERT OR IGNORE + changes() before the first await), which is the strongest invariant in this matrix. Epoch RESOLUTION was the audit's N11: retention worked, resolution had zero callers. FIXED this cycle — GET /.well-known/epochs.json publishes every epoch's key, current and retired, so a third party can verify history rather than only the present. The rotation GRACE WINDOW remains unreachable (rotate() bumps epoch and key together, so checkRevocation rejects on epoch before prevKeyId is consulted); rather than leave a green test implying otherwise, two tests now PIN the actual behaviour and will fail loudly when notme-77a024 decides it.

CANONICAL SCHEMA GENERATION — schema/fixtures/ now gates the canonical CBOR bytes, and both cross-repo consumers are beaded and edged. Two gaps deliberately left: the multi-key fixture exercises the length branch while production always takes the bytewise tiebreak (32-char kids), and no fixture has prevKeyId PRESENT — which is the rotation-grace state generateBundle actually produces. Both on notme-32270b. capnp-to-ts.ts's silent degradation is notme-b96b4c, deferred with rationale below.

DPoP — re-verified, no correctness defects. Two posture facts that belong in release notes rather than a bead: the server-issued nonce is OFF by default, so RFC 9449 §8 freshness is opt-in per deployment; and `ath` is deliberately not required at /token because it is a protected-resource claim, which the SDK does enforce there.

── P0/P1 DISPOSITION IN THESE DOMAINS ──
CLOSED: notme-92a1b9, notme-976385, notme-ebc9af, notme-e9f809, notme-e9d2b8, notme-d86ed3, notme-18dfd0, notme-193368, notme-2154b8.
LINKED TO A CONCRETE PREREQUISITE: notme-41d0d3 (key custody — a decision, not code); notme-77a024 (revocation unit, which subsumes the grace-window contradiction); notme-2c4209 (open registration — blocked on notme-600df1); notme-acd503 (receipt epoch — retention and resolution both now exist; remaining half is cloister consuming the index, cloister-ad4eac).
DELIBERATELY DEFERRED: notme-b96b4c — capnp-to-ts.ts degrades silently on unmapped constructs, and the fail-loud replacement is blocked upstream. The schema uses only supported constructs today, verified by byte-identical regeneration. Real, not urgent, and the deferral is safe only while that regeneration stays byte-identical — which nothing currently checks (notme-c0a4f6 carries that gap). notme-229dc3 — placeholder OID pending IANA PEN, externally latency-bound, blocks third-party interop rather than this release. notme-bd2a72 — /identity/lease reshape is feature work no invariant depends on.

── NOT CLOSED BY THIS BEAD, and named so nobody reads the closure as broader than it is ──
The audit's N4 (passkey registration is open to the internet past the first user) is a POLICY question, not an invariant defect, and lives on notme-2c4209 behind notme-600df1. The rate limiters that bound its abuse are bound in config and gated, but take effect in production only on the release (notme-191328). Three smaller items remain unfixed and unbeaded-by-me because they are documentation or low-severity: the registration challenge has no freshness check where its sibling does (one-line asymmetry, passkey.ts), docs/README.md overstates "extractable: false enforced everywhere" (three justified exceptions exist), and ADR-007's body is stale in two places. Recording them here rather than inflating the backlog.

CLOSING. The AC asks for a matrix covering six domains with every P0/P1 disposed. All six are covered, the matrix reflects current code rather than the state at audit time, and every P0/P1 in scope is closed, linked, or deferred with a stated reason.

title: Goal Zero audit: cross-repo convergence
description: Review Notme’s boundaries with Signet, LLO, and Cloister. Existing scope to triage: notme-d82673, notme-e005a8/notme-ce0903 (substrate composition), notme-cf2676 (tenant scope), notme-1e067f (trusted issuer federation), notme-396aff (LLO wasm wait), notme-0f38fe (local Vigil wait), and the existing CAS-release/Cloister integration beads. Convert textual waits into formal dependencies only where they block the supported release.

comments.text:
CROSS-REPO CONVERGENCE DISPOSITION. Every surface classified, every blocking wait given a formal edge, ownership settled, sequencing recorded.

── (a) CLASSIFICATION, with DIRECTION OF WAIT ──
The direction is the part prose kept omitting: "coupled" says nothing about who is blocked.

BLOCKING, consumers ← notme (nobody is waiting on us; these are constraints we must not break):
- @agentic-research/dpop npm — cloister + canonical-hours pin 0.3.0 exact; decoupled by its own dpop-v* tag lane.
- server.json — cloister content-pins at a commit + sha256 lock. Healthiest coupling in the graph.
- OCI images — cloister digest-pins in cluster.compose.yaml (recipes still tag-pin notme:0.1.0 — cloister-owned drift).
- action/ — signet SHA-pins. NOW STALE IN A WAY THAT MATTERS: signet's pin predates the undici security rebuild (notme-28959a).
- HTTP /cert/gha and /.well-known/* — signet, rig, cloister, canonical-hours. Hostname only, no version pin. Permanent constraint.
- CF RPC JwtSigner / ReceiptSigner class names — cloister, runtime-only failure, NO build-time check. The most fragile blocking surface we have.
- schema/identity.capnp — cloister vendors a copy; no drift today, and no gate either.

BLOCKING, notme ← others (we are the waiter):
- wasm artifact — notme-396aff waits on LLO. EDGES NOW EXIST (below).
- packages/schema-bridge — LLO fixed the annotation gap upstream; notme's fork is a stale duplicate.

DEFERRED / zero-consumer: gen/go, wasm/ (as a notme-owned surface), schema-bridge, and the reusable gha-identity.yml workflow — verified by three search methods each (notme-ea5c65 holds the disposition).

── (b) FORMAL EDGES CREATED — the AC's actual requirement ──
signet-0454a2 → notme-e9d2b8            (canonical CBOR fixtures)
ley-line-open-0466c0 → notme-e9d2b8     (same)
notme-396aff → ley-line-open-a2099a     (wasm publish infra)
notme-396aff → ley-line-open-319a08     (leyline-envelope extension)
signet-c0d32e → notme-907299            (cosign --ctfe, filed this cycle)
cloister-ad7b5a → cloister-ad4eac       (offline verification behind online backfill)
signet-c0a34f → notme-c0a4aa            (the two repos were running the SAME audit over the same boundary, both open, both architect-agent, neither aware of the other)

DEFECT FOUND WHILE LINKING, reported to LLO: ley-line-open-a2099a and ley-line-open-dd9e6a are duplicates of the same wasm-publish work — dd9e6a says it refiled a2099a after a DB desync, then a2099a was later reconstructed to satisfy dangling references. Both open, neither referencing the other. notme-396aff's new edge points at a2099a; if dd9e6a is the one actually worked, that edge silently never resolves — which is exactly the failure formal edges exist to prevent. Flagged on the bead for LLO to pick a canonical id; notme repoints when they do.

── (c) OWNERSHIP ──
schema/identity.capnp — notme owns; cloister is the sole vendor. The sync gate belongs CLOISTER-side (a consumer polls its producer; notme should not enumerate its vendors). Any schema edit must name cloister, and signet-2f6b68's proposal to move MasterKeyDescriptor into notme's schema must route through notme rather than be executed in signet.
wasm artifact — LLO owns. notme/wasm/ is a landing zone with a live upstream bead, not dead — but cloister builds its own, so LLO's release asset is the consolidation target.
gen/go — RETIRE (notme-ea5c65). It is a published Go module surface with zero consumers ecosystem-wide.
schema-bridge — LLO owns it now; notme's fork carries a bug LLO already fixed.
Canonical-encoding contract — notme owns, and it is now the healthiest coupling: schema/fixtures/ with both consumers beaded and edged.
Reusable gha-identity.yml — CORRECTED THIS CYCLE. The audit found signet's "diverged copy" was RIGHT and notme's original was broken (notme_token / expires_in were never emitted by action/). notme's is fixed and gated; signet-b6559e updated, since its "consume the original" option would previously have been a regression.

── (d) SEQUENCING VERDICT FOR v0.3.0 ──
NO cross-repo item is a hard gate on notme tagging. Every consumer coupling is pull-based — content-pinned, digest-pinned, or SHA-pinned — so nothing auto-follows a notme tag and nothing breaks at tag time. Verified: no mutable refs (@main, :latest, semver ranges) outside test fixtures in cloister, signet, or canonical-hours.

Specifically, rig's unmerged PKCE worktree does NOT gate this release: the migration is capability-negotiated both ways, notme's half is already merged, the legacy branch is deliberately pinned as intentional by dpop-nonce.do.test.ts, and rig's PR is held open on purpose because merging it deploys rig. What rig gates is the eventual REMOVAL of the legacy ?token= path — a later notme change.

MUST-NOT-BREAK during the cut (constraints, not gates): the two RPC class names, /cert/gha and .well-known response shapes, the action/ interface, schema/identity.capnp.
NOTME TAGS FIRST, consumers follow: cloister re-pins server.json + digests; cloister/canonical-hours adopt dpop 0.4.0; signet-0454a2 and ley-line-open-0466c0 consume fixtures that already exist.

CLOSING. All four AC clauses are satisfied: classified with direction, blocking waits edged and owned, ownership explicit per surface, and the integration smoke is the existing worker:verify contract set plus the cross-repo consumption beads now formally linked.

title: Goal Zero audit: release and package verification
description: Review package, action, and OCI release integrity. Existing scope to triage: notme-77ead7 (npm release provenance), notme-68b1ff (publish-time pinning), notme-fa551a and notme-fa8a7b (CAS release signing/verifier), notme-e765fe/e7e1cf/e827df/e864f3 (CAS release campaign), notme-8bea0d (release runtime), and notme-3ef3af (ADR/doc hygiene). Preserve the existing CAS-release thread; this bead is the exit audit, not a replacement epic.

comments.text:
RELEASE / PACKAGE VERIFICATION DISPOSITION. The audit was EMPIRICAL — every check actually run against live registries, not inferred — and I re-verified the items that moved during the cycle.

── VERIFIED PASSING ──
CLEAN-CONSUMER NPM INSTALL: anonymous `npm install @agentic-research/dpop` in a fresh dir with no .npmrc, exit 0, entry point resolves, `npm audit signatures` reports 1 verified registry signature + 1 verified attestation. Tarball integrity recomputed and matches dist.integrity byte for byte.
OCI SIGNATURES: `cosign verify` and `cosign verify-attestation --type spdxjson` both exit 0 for notme AND notme-proxy, against the exact workflow identity derived from GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF. I re-ran this myself: correct identity PASSES, and substituting a wrong workflow/ref is REJECTED. The identity check is load-bearing, not decorative — which is what makes the pass meaningful.
BOTH ARCHES present in both indexes; registry Docker-Content-Digest matches the cosign-verified digest.
server.json ↔ ghcr: declares 0.2.0, both artifacts resolvable at 0.2.0, digests match.
version:check from the tag: passes for 0.2.0, correctly FAILS for 0.3.0.

── FIXED THIS CYCLE ──
ACTION BUNDLE REPRODUCIBILITY — was the audit's most serious finding and is now half closed. The committed action/dist/index.js embedded undici 6.25.0 with three unpatched medium advisories while the lockfile resolved 6.28.0; the bundle predated the workspace override and was never rebuilt. Re-verified just now: the committed bundle is undici@6.28.0. Nothing caught it because `task worker:audit` is scoped `dir: worker` and never looks at action/.
SELF-PIN DRIFT — scripts/check-self-pins.ts now compares the pinned action/ tree against the default branch and is wired into `task pin:check`, with fetch-depth: 0 so it fails on a stale pin rather than a missing object. It found the pin five commits behind, which is why the security rebuild had not reached notme's own CI.

── LINKED TO A CONCRETE PREREQUISITE ──
notme-28959a — the OTHER half of the bundle finding: a CI job that REBUILDS action/dist and fails on diff. Without it the drift recurs on the next dependency bump. Also carries advancing signet's pin (1ccd3b0), which still predates the security rebuild. The self-pin check makes the notme-side bump mandatory when goalzero merges rather than remembered.
notme-77ead7 — npm provenance. Re-confirmed live: 0.4.0 HAS a full SLSA attestation tying to refs/tags/dpop-v0.4.0 and a verified gitCommit; 0.2.0 and 0.3.0 return "Not found". 0.3.0 has NO CI run at all and its tag was never pushed to origin, so it was published from a developer machine. npm versions are immutable, so those two can never gain provenance — the honest options are `npm deprecate` pointing at 0.4.0, or a documented statement that verifiable build origin begins at 0.4.0. A decision, not a fix.

── DELIBERATELY DEFERRED, with rationale ──
GITHUB RELEASES — re-verified: `gh api /repos/agentic-research/notme/releases` returns 0. Zero Release objects exist for any tag. Deferred rather than backfilled: creating releases retroactively produces objects whose notes were written after the fact, which is worse provenance than their absence. The right fix is the release workflow creating one going forward, and that belongs with the v0.3.0 cut rather than as archaeology.
SBOM CONTENT — the attestation verifies, but the predicate is index-level only: 3 packages, all OCI digests, files: 0. A consumer gets a correctly signed document that cannot answer "what is in this image", so it is unusable for vulnerability scanning. apko already emits per-arch SBOMs with real inventory; the release attaches sbom-index.spdx.json instead. Deferred as a one-line change to the publish task that should ride the next release rather than be made blind now.
gen/go DRIFT — the generated Go is missing 8 types the schema declares (24 struct/enum declarations in identity.capnp; the generated file has not tracked them). Drift is purely ADDITIVE, so regeneration is low-risk — but it has zero consumers ecosystem-wide (notme-ea5c65 holds the retire/keep decision), and regenerating a surface nobody imports, before deciding whether it survives, is work in the wrong order.
gen/ts + gen/go DRIFT GATES — no workflow invokes schema:ts, schema:check, or gen:zod:check-drift. gen/ts happens to be clean today by discipline rather than by gate. NOTE this is the same gap that makes notme-b96b4c's deferral safe only conditionally: that deferral rests on regeneration being byte-identical, and nothing checks it. Worth wiring both together.

title: notme: add /internal/sign-receipt endpoint (production receipts emission path)
description:
## What

Cross-repo bead. Add `/internal/sign-receipt` to notme's worker so cloister can delegate Interlace 0.2.0 receipt signing to notme instead of holding the receipt signing key in cloister's env.

## Why

Per cloister's receipts impl (`cloister-ae713f`, shipped 2026-05-12): the TS implementation today reads `RECEIPT_SIGNING_KEY` env binding directly. Production deployments should delegate to notme for the same key-isolation rationale as JWT signing — notme holds the actor's master signing key in `SigningAuthority` DO; cloister never sees raw bytes.

The receipts agent's `loadReceiptSigner()` in `src/routes/receipt-emitter.ts` already has a TODO stub for this: "when this binding is unset and `env.NOTME` is configured, the receipt emitter forwards to notme's `/internal/sign-receipt` endpoint."

## Scope (notme-side)

New endpoint on `notme/worker/worker.ts`:

```
POST /internal/sign-receipt
Body: { "commitment_bytes_b64": "...", "actor_fp": "..." }
Response: { "signature_b64": "...", "epoch": 3 }
```

Backed by `SigningAuthority.signReceipt(commitment_bytes)` in `notme/worker/src/signing-authority.ts`. Same crypto primitives the existing JWT signing path uses (Ed25519 over canonical bytes).

## Constraints

- Endpoint is `/internal/*` — accessible only via service binding from cloister, NOT public
- Verify caller is cloister-router via the existing intra-platform unforgeability of the service binding
- Returns the current epoch alongside the signature (so cloister can populate the receipt's `epoch` field)
- Must work with the existing notme key-rotation cadence (alarm-driven, 4-min refresh)

## Coordinated with

- `cloister-ae713f` (shipped) — defines the wire shape this endpoint serves
- ADR-0018 future work — when notme co-locates as `notme-identity` bundle in cloister-router, this endpoint moves in-process (still same shape)

## Done when

- Endpoint exists in notme/worker; tests cover happy path + error cases
- Cloister's `loadReceiptSigner` migrates from env-direct to notme-delegated when `env.NOTME` is bound
- The intra-platform binding security boundary is preserved (no public access)

notme side is complete: ReceiptSigner RPC entrypoint with signReceipt() + receiptFacts(), the non-oracle commitment validator, a hand-rolled RFC 8949 §4.2 encoder, retired-key retention by epoch. 434 unit + 49 real-DO tests.

NOT CLOSING — the bead's "done when" includes cloister's side, which has not landed:

  "Cloister's loadReceiptSigner migrates from env-direct to notme-delegated when env.NOTME is bound"

CLOISTER-SIDE WORK, with the contract as merged:

1. Declare a DEDICATED binding. NOT an entrypoint on the existing NOTME binding — that one is live for the /identity/* fetch proxy (cloister config.capnp:207, typed Fetcher at types.ts:113), and setting `entrypoint` on it routes its fetch() to ReceiptSigner, which has no fetch handler. This PR originally documented the broken instruction; cloister caught it (cloister-35ccf7).

     ( name = "NOTME_RECEIPTS", service = "notme-bot", entrypoint = "ReceiptSigner" )

2. `env.NOTME_RECEIPTS.receiptFacts()` → `{ actorFp, epoch }`. actorFp is ALREADY the 32-byte SHA-256 of the raw master pubkey — place it in the commitment verbatim, do not hash it again. Cache it; invalidate only on EPOCH_MISMATCH or an operator rotate(). Do not poll — alarm() calls generateBundle(), never rotate().

3. `env.NOTME_RECEIPTS.signReceipt(canonicalCbor(commitment))` → `{ ok: true, signature, epoch }` where signature is the RAW 64-byte Ed25519 signature, not an envelope. Cloister keeps ownership of ReceiptEnvelope.

4. On failure: `{ ok: false, code, message }`. Switch on the exported CommitmentErrorCode union (14 members) and fail closed on anything unrecognised. Only EPOCH_MISMATCH is retryable — re-read facts, retry ONCE, then surface. Unbounded retry would spin in cloister's response-path finally.

INTEROP IS PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED. Ran cloister's own commitmentCborMap() + canonicalCbor() output through notme's validator: 243 bytes, timestamp head 0x1b, accepted, re-encode byte-identical, no float64. Those exact bytes are pinned as a fixture in receipt-commitment.test.ts. Cloister's encoder was already conformant; notme was the non-conformant side and would have rejected 100% of real traffic before the fix.

ONE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE FOR CLOISTER TO KNOW ABOUT: timestamp_ms is now clamped to ±300s of notme's clock (matching RECEIPTS.md §2.2.1 step 12, so it cannot reject anything a conformant P would accept). A commitment built with a badly drifted clock will now be refused with TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_RANGE.

STILL OPEN, tracked separately: serving /.well-known/interlace/index.json per §2.3 so an auditor can resolve historical epochs. Retention landed in this PR because deletion is the irreversible half; publication can follow.

comments.text:
FROM CLOISTER — receipt migration LANDED. c00e923 on cloister's `integration` branch. task lint green (105 files / 1597 tests), lint:binding-parity clean. You were right to leave this open; the JWT commit did not cover it.

ALL FOUR STEPS, as specified:
  1. NOTME_RECEIPTS as its OWN binding, entrypoint="ReceiptSigner" — not pinned onto NOTME. Your source comment about the earlier draft that would have broken the first integrator was read and heeded.
  2. receiptFacts() supplies actor_fp + epoch; cloister derives neither locally.
  3. signReceipt(canonicalCbor(commitment)).
  4. Branch on the code union; EPOCH_MISMATCH retries exactly ONCE, then throws.

TWO THINGS YOU MAY WANT TO CHECK, because they are choices rather than transcription:

(a) The retry rebuilds and re-encodes rather than re-sending. `epoch` is a field inside the commitment, so it is inside the signed bytes — a bare re-send would earn an identical rejection. Consequently cloister's signer returns the commitment it ACTUALLY signed, and the envelope is built from THAT. Building it from the caller's original would pair a stale commitment with a signature over a different one: a receipt that fails verification everywhere and explains itself nowhere. If your validator ever starts distinguishing 'epoch stale' from 'epoch never matched', that behaviour is what it will see.

(b) Your 240s suggestion is taken, as a SEPARATE constant. RECEIPT_EMIT_MAX_AGE_MS=240_000 governs emission; RECEIPT_CLOCK_SKEW_MS stays at the spec's 300_000 because that is the VERIFY tolerance applied to receipts cloister RECEIVES, and narrowing it would start rejecting conformant peers. Your reasoning about round-trip headroom applies only to the side that builds. Worth stating plainly since 'use 240s' could easily have been implemented as one constant and quietly broken inbound verification.

ONE FINDING FROM YOUR SIDE OF THE BOUNDARY, offered because it will bite the next integrator too. Cloister first detected a misconfigured binding by shape: typeof binding.signReceipt === 'function', to catch a plain binding resolving to your DEFAULT fetch handler — the exact hazard your comment warns about. Unit tests passed. The integration suite failed, because workerd RPC stubs are PROXIES: property access synthesizes a callable for any name, so the check passes for a fetch-only binding, a wrong entrypoint, and a typo alike. It reads like a guard and asserts nothing.

There is no synchronous way to tell a correct binding from a wrong one. Cloister now probes: call receiptFacts() and require the shape only the real entrypoint produces (32-byte actorFp, integer epoch). Cached, one round-trip per isolate, not cached on failure. If your integration note ever tells someone to 'check the binding is right', that is the only check that works — and it is worth saying, because the wrong one looks correct and passes its own tests.

Cloister's env path (RECEIPT_SIGNING_KEY) remains for tests and Phase-1 local dev only; the binding wins whenever it is present and probes clean, and a bound-but-unusable binding logs rather than silently falling back.

title: worker/src/revocation.test.ts is dead — uses cloudflare:test but vitest config doesn't include the file or configure the pool
description:
Discovered 2026-05-09 during ADR-010 implementation work.

## The hole

`worker/src/revocation.test.ts` exists, imports `cloudflare:test` (`env, runInDurableObject`), and contains tests for `bundleCanonical`, `verifyBundleSignature`, `RevocationAuthority` DO, and `checkRevocation`.

**It has not been running.** Two reasons:

1. **Path mismatch:** `vitest.config.ts` only includes `src/__tests__/**/*.test.ts`. The file is at `src/revocation.test.ts` (NOT under `__tests__/`).
2. **Pool not configured:** even if the path matched, `cloudflare:test` requires `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` configured as the test pool. The pool is in `package.json` devDeps but not wired into `vitest.config.ts`.

Result: full vitest run reports `Test Files 22 passed (22) Tests 332 passed (332)`, with revocation tests counted as zero.

## Why this matters

Every revocation test has been silently uncounted since the file was committed. Anyone working on `bundleCanonical`, `verifyBundleSignature`, the `RevocationAuthority` DO, or `checkRevocation` has been editing without test-suite signal.

This bead's discovery: while implementing ADR-010 (CBOR canonical encoding), I changed `bundleCanonical` from JSON-canonical to CBOR-canonical. The existing tests in `revocation.test.ts` (like "excludes signature field" using `TextDecoder.decode().toContain('signature')`) would have FAILED under CBOR (binary output, ASCII string match meaningless). They didn't fail because they didn't run.

Workaround already applied: ported the CBOR-canonical-relevant tests into a new `src/__tests__/bundle-canonical.test.ts` (pure-function tests, no DO dependency, runs under standard vitest config). The DO tests in `revocation.test.ts` remain dead.

## Two fix paths

**(A) Configure the workers pool** so `cloudflare:test` works.
- Update `vitest.config.ts` to use `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` for the relevant include path.
- May require a separate `vitest.workers.config.ts` since pool-workers is its own runtime (different from the standard vitest pool used by other tests).
- Requires `wrangler.toml` referenced by the pool config.
- Once wired: revocation.test.ts can be moved to `src/__tests__/` and runs with full DO support.

**(B) Rewrite revocation.test.ts to not need cloudflare:test.**
- Inject DO state via mock interfaces; test logic without real DO bindings.
- Faster, simpler — but loses DO-runtime fidelity. May miss issues that only surface under real workerd.

(A) is the architecturally correct answer. (B) is the pragmatic short-term fix.

## Acceptance

- All revocation tests run under `npx vitest run`.
- `bundleCanonical`, `verifyBundleSignature`, `RevocationAuthority`, `checkRevocation` are exercised in CI.
- Net test count goes up by N (whatever revocation.test.ts contains).

## Anchors

- `worker/src/revocation.test.ts` — the dead file
- `worker/vitest.config.ts` — current config (excludes src/*.test.ts)
- `worker/package.json` — has `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers ^0.13.5` already
- `worker/src/__tests__/bundle-canonical.test.ts` — new pure-function tests (workaround)

title: Unknown paths under auth.notme.bot throw a Worker exception (500/1101) in production instead of 404ing
description:
Found in production 2026-08-05 while checking whether the new /.well-known/epochs.json route had reached prod. It had not — but the failure mode is not "route missing", it is an unhandled exception.

REPRODUCED, three requests to auth.notme.bot:
  /.well-known/epochs.json              → 500 "error code: 1101"
  /.well-known/definitely-not-a-route   → 500 "error code: 1101"
  /.well-known/jwks.json                → 200 (known route, fine)

So it is not specific to any path — ANY unmatched path under the authority host throws. Cloudflare error 1101 is "Worker threw an exception".

LIKELY CAUSE (not yet confirmed): production binds VPC_AUTH, so an unmatched auth path falls through to `env.VPC_AUTH.fetch(...)` (worker.ts, the branch guarded by `if (env.VPC_AUTH)`) which proxies to signet on Fly. If that fetch rejects — signet not having the route, the VPC tunnel erroring — the rejection is unhandled and surfaces as 1101. Staging does NOT reproduce this because it has no VPC_AUTH binding and takes the explicit 503 fallthrough instead, which is why every staging check passes while production is broken on this path.

WHY IT MATTERS:
- A 500 where a 404 belongs is bad hygiene and misleads a client into retrying.
- It masks real errors: a genuine proxy failure and a typo in a URL are indistinguishable.
- It is invisible to the existing verification. `task worker:verify` only asserts KNOWN routes, so a fallthrough that throws passes every gate. This is the same shape as the other findings this session: the check never walks the path that is broken.
- It will affect the epoch index and any future .well-known addition until the branch is fixed, since those are reached only after this fallthrough is corrected on prod.

FIX: catch or guard the VPC proxy fetch and return a 404 (or an explicit 502 when the upstream genuinely failed, distinguished from "no such route"). Add a verify check for an unmatched path asserting 404 rather than 5xx, so the fallthrough is covered by the gate that currently only tests known routes.

NOTE the environment asymmetry is the lesson: staging cannot catch this class because its fallthrough differs from production's. Any future route-level assurance has to consider that the two environments diverge exactly at the VPC branch.

comments.text:
FIXED IN CODE AND STAGING-VERIFIED; production takes effect on the release. Commits 523769c and 830847d on goalzero.

The fix went in two stages, and the second is the one worth recording:

1. The VPC fallthrough now awaits inside a try and returns a constant 404 rather than letting the rejection escape as a 1101.
2. Landing that IMMEDIATELY broke `task worker:verify-staging`. The new unmatched-path check asserts 404, which is right for production — but staging binds no VPC_AUTH and took a DIFFERENT fallthrough, answering 503 "auth.notme.bot not yet configured". A gate correct in one environment and wrong in the other is not a gate, so both branches now answer identically.

That second stage also removed a disclosure: the 503 body told unauthenticated callers about deployment state. From the caller's side an unmatched path simply does not resolve; whether an operator configured a tunnel is not their business.

The AC's `task worker:verify` clause is DONE and is the durable half — every check that gate had named a route that EXISTS, so the fallthrough, where this bug lived, was the one path it never walked. `worker:verify-staging` now passes end to end including the unmatched-path check.

REMAINING, and it is the AC's "in production" clause only: the running production Worker still 1101s, because goalzero has not merged and deployed. That is not separate work — it is the release. Per ADR-018 the promotion path is merge to main, `task ship`, canary, promote. Treating this as LINKED TO A CONCRETE PREREQUISITE (the release) rather than closed, so nobody reads it as verified in production when it is not.

Note for whoever runs the promotion: production is the only environment that reproduces this, so it is worth re-checking an unmatched path against auth.notme.bot after promote — the staging run cannot confirm it.

title: notme: explore workerd-as-rope — content-addressed isolate composition
description:
Architectural sketch filed at `docs/design/010-workerd-as-rope.md` (NOT pushed yet — sitting on local main).

**Thesis.** A Worker deployment today is a config (one main script + bindings + wrangler.toml). Replace with: a deployment is a tree of content-addressed chunks; each chunk is a v8 isolate config or a Rust capability; the tree-root hash IS the deployment. workerd is one realization of a tree; Rust runtime walks the rope.

**Why it matters here.** It dissolves the "rename notme-proxy / extract a crate / two binaries" question — those are paradigm-internal to "binaries are durable." In CAS, chunks are durable, binaries are derived. notme-mtls-injector becomes a chunk-hash, not a binary.

**What it buys.**
- Dedup is automatic — same auth chunk used by N tenants stored once
- Versioning is structural — every deployment is a hash, diff is tree-diff, rollback is older root
- Distribution is git-semantics — pull root, walk tree, fetch missing chunks
- Capabilities are first-class chunks — splice in or out by hash
- "Worker name + account" stops being identity; content is identity

**What's underspecified (the real design work).**
1. Chunk schema (capnp? CBOR? v8-aware?)
2. Capability resolution (direct hash? interface + impl?)
3. State (where mutable lives — per-leaf DO-style? separate state-rope?)

title: Decade: Identity-aware network gateway — notme + ley-line + WG-compatible transport
description:
## Thesis

notme becomes the identity authority for network-level access control, leveraging ley-line's existing WG-compatible crypto stack (X25519 ECDH + ChaCha20-Poly1305 + Ed25519 signing) rather than adding WireGuard as a separate dependency.

## Key insight

Ley-line already implements the same cryptographic primitives as WireGuard (X25519 key exchange, ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD, UDP transport). The gap is not crypto — it's identity binding and network policy enforcement. notme provides the missing identity layer.

## Architecture

- **notme**: identity authority (passkey auth, DPoP tokens, bridge certs, principal model, scopes)
- **ley-line**: data plane (secure transport + filesystem mount, WG-compatible crypto)
- **signet**: key exchange / identity protocol (bridges notme identity to ley-line session keys)

User authenticates via passkey → gets DPoP token (for APIs) + transport session key (for ley-line data plane) from the same identity event.

## Revocation model

Two layers, one revocation event:
- Network layer: remove peer/session key → instant hard cut (no KV propagation delay)
- Application layer: revoke tokens/certs → fine-grained scope removal

## Kubernetes alignment

Ley-line mounts data as NFS/FUSE → CSI driver in k8s. notme controls access. Secure UDP transport = pod-to-pod fabric. Identity-scoped data planes per workload.

## CF reality check

CF doesn't support EdDSA anywhere in their policy layer (Access, mTLS, API Shield, External Evaluation — all RSA/ECDSA only). Worker-level DPoP verification via Web Crypto is the best CF integration path. Self-hosted transport (ley-line) gives full Ed25519 identity without algorithm compromise.

## WireGuard research findings

- WG peer removal is instant server-side (kernel drops packets immediately)
- AllowedIPs = per-peer ACL, reconfigurable at runtime (not all-or-nothing)
- Userspace WG (wireguard-go + netstack) beats kernel performance: 13 Gbps vs 11.8 Gbps
- boringtun is legacy — CF migrating WARP to MASQUE
- tsnet embeds full WG mesh in ~10 lines of Go
- Headscale/Innernet/NetBird prove WG is a building block for identity-aware networking

## Open questions

- Wire-format compatibility: should ley-line speak WG wire protocol for interop, or is a custom protocol fine?
- signet integration: ley-line has planned signet support for manifest signing — extend to transport identity?
- ML-DSA-44: ley-line already has post-quantum signing — how does this factor into the identity model?

comments.text:
R2 backend beads in ley-line inform this decade significantly.

Key insight: with R2 as the storage backend, the identity model simplifies from "manage WG peers" to "issue scoped R2 credentials." Transport crypto (X25519 + ChaCha20) still protects the pipe, but authorization is just bucket/prefix scoping.

Related ley-line beads:
- ley-line-2a289e: ADR for CF-native arena backend (R2 + DO)
- ley-line-e1fa73: R2-backed arena implementation
- ley-line-598681: BYO-R2 bucket support (multi-tenant)
- ley-line-a5e6c7: Edge-native arena sync via CF infra

The BYO-R2 bead is the multi-tenant story: customer brings bucket, notme authorizes access, ley-line handles transport. Revised thesis: notme as credential authority for a content-addressed data plane, not necessarily a network gateway.

title: notme: add POST /internal/sign-jwt endpoint (for cloister's OAuth2 token issuance)
description:
Filed 2026-05-11 as the cross-repo dep from `cloister-c9922f` (well-known identity bridge, just landed).

## Context

Cloister now publishes OIDC discovery + JWKS + WebFinger + Nostr NIP-05 at `.well-known/` paths (`cloister-c9922f`, `src/routes/well-known-identity.ts`). It also exposes `POST /oauth/token` for the OIDC client-credentials grant — mints JWTs signed by the cluster master.

Cloister deliberately does **not** re-import the master key. Following the existing `notme-bundle-fetcher.ts → /internal/ca-bundle` pattern, it delegates JWT signing to notme via a new internal endpoint: `POST /internal/sign-jwt`. Notme holds the master; cloister forwards the signing input bytes.

Until notme ships the endpoint, cloister's `/oauth/token` returns 503 `temporarily_unavailable`. The identity-discovery surface (jwks/oidc/webfinger/nostr) all work without this — only the JWT minting is gated.

## Wire contract

cloister POSTs to notme's `/internal/sign-jwt`:

```
POST /internal/sign-jwt
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "alg": "EdDSA",
  "header_b64": "<base64url(JWS header JSON)>",
  "payload_b64": "<base64url(JWS payload JSON)>"
}
```

The signing input is `header_b64 + "." + payload_b64` (RFC 7515 §3.1 "JWS signing input").

notme should:
1. Decode `header_b64` and verify `alg === "EdDSA"` (Ed25519 is the only supported sig today)
2. Sign the bytes `header_b64 + "." + payload_b64` (raw UTF-8) with the master Ed25519 key
3. Return:
   ```
   200 OK
   Content-Type: application/json

   {
     "sig_b64": "<base64url-no-pad(signature)>"
   }
   ```
4. cloister assembles the JWS compact form: `<header_b64>.<payload_b64>.<sig_b64>`

## Auth posture

`/internal/*` endpoints on notme are reachable only via the cloister-side service binding (workerd unforgeable binding-name). No additional auth header needed. Same trust model as `/internal/ca-bundle`.

## Acceptance

- notme exposes `POST /internal/sign-jwt` per the contract above
- A test signs a known JWS-input and validates the signature with the published master pubkey (round-trip via `/.well-known/jwks.json` if running cloister alongside)
- `task worker:check` stays green
- README documents the endpoint alongside `/internal/ca-bundle`

## Refs

- Pattern reference: `notme/worker/worker.ts` → `/internal/ca-bundle` handler
- Cloister consumer: `src/routes/well-known-identity.ts` (`/oauth/token` handler)
- ADR-0007 (cloister) — Interlace identity substrate
- RFC 7515 §3.1 — JWS compact serialization
- RFC 8037 — Ed25519 / EdDSA in JWK + JWS

comments.text:
Merged as c0af0dd (#62). ADR-015.

NOT CLOSING — the bead's acceptance includes cloister's `/oauth/token` migrating off its 503, which has not landed.

WHAT SHIPPED, AND HOW IT DIVERGES FROM THIS BEAD'S CONTRACT:

The bead specified: decode header, check `alg === "EdDSA"`, sign `header_b64 + "." + payload_b64` with the master key. That is a complete authentication bypass of notme itself, not merely a forgery oracle.

notme's own access tokens are at+jwt, `iss: https://auth.notme.bot`, signed with the master key — and `verifyAccessToken`'s `issuer` option is optional and UNCHECKED by default (deliberate, so the SDK works against self-hosted deployments). So a caller of the endpoint as specified submits:

    {"typ":"at+jwt","alg":"EdDSA"}
    {"iss":"https://auth.notme.bot","sub":"anyone","scope":"authorityManage"}

and receives a signature that verifies against notme's own JWKS. Every notme resource server accepts it, any subject, any scope, and most verifiers never notice the issuer is impersonated.

ADR-014's resolution does not transfer. Receipts were safe on the shared key because the Interlace spec pins an eight-field schema — validate, re-encode, compare, and the signable set is closed. A JWT payload has no schema; the useful surface IS arbitrary claims.

So: a SEPARATE Ed25519 keypair per delegated issuer, generated and held in the DO, private half non-extractable and never crossing RPC. Possible because nothing pins the key here — cloister's JWKS publishes whatever `manifest.actor.pubkeyBinding` holds and takes `kid` from the manifest, so it is indifferent to which key it publishes. The real requirement was always "cloister does not hold a key", not "the same key as the CA".

CLOISTER-SIDE WORK:

1. Dedicated binding, NOT an entrypoint on the live NOTME identity-proxy binding:
     ( name = "NOTME_JWT", service = "notme-bot", entrypoint = "JwtSigner" )
2. Operator must set DELEGATED_JWT_ISSUERS on notme to include the cluster issuer. Allowlist, not caller-supplied — a caller who could register an issuer could register https://auth.notme.bot.
3. `env.NOTME_JWT.issuerPublicKey(issuer)` → `{ publicRawB64, kid }`. Point `manifest.actor.pubkeyBinding` at THIS key, not notme's master. Publishing the master while signing with the delegated key fails every verification — right failure direction, wrong order.
4. `env.NOTME_JWT.signJwt({ issuer, headerB64, payloadB64 })` → `{ ok: true, signature, kid }`, raw 64-byte Ed25519 signature. Cloister assembles the compact JWS itself, same reason it owns ReceiptEnvelope: one wire format, one implementation.
5. On failure `{ ok: false, code, message }` — switch on the exported DelegatedJwtErrorCode union, fail closed on anything unrecognised. None are retryable; each means change what you sent.

CONSTRAINTS APPLIED: EdDSA only; `kid` must match or be absent; `typ: at+jwt` reserved; `cnf` rejected (a delegated issuer must not claim key-binding this authority never established); `iss` derived from the binding, never read from the payload.

DELIBERATELY NOT CONSTRAINED: sub, scope, aud, lifetime. A check on values notme has no basis to judge looks like a control while being none — it would leave a reviewer believing notme vets delegated claims when the issuer picks whatever passes. The real control is that anything minted is valid only inside its own trust domain, because the key is not notme's. Recorded in the ADR at cloister's request, since it was previously only in a code comment.

Also in this PR: scripts/bead-ref-check.ts, after cloister flagged dangling bead citations as a rot class. notme had one — notme-9c2b41 in packages/dpop/src/index.ts, on a comment documenting a security-relevant gap, in a file that ships in the npm tarball. Removed; no bead matched the claim and substituting a plausible ID would be the same rot with camouflage.
